**Ivar Evil-Eye** was a former member of the Order of Witchers and the School of the Bear. He later founded the School of the Viper. 

## Biography[]

Nothing is known about his life before he became a witcher.

## Biography[]

Nothing is known about his life before he became a witcher. 

When Ivar underwent the mutations, he responded exceptionally well and was selected for further, more complex experiments. Out of those chosen, he was the only one to survive because the mages were only able to complete the trial partially. As a result of these experiments, he gained his "Evil Eye," which would give him his moniker. His left eye allowed him to see various other worlds, leading him to discover the Wild Hunt. He witnessed them dash along the Spiral from world to world, killing, conquering, and kidnapping as they went. These visions became an obsession for him.[2]

When the witcher Arnaghad led a posse of his fellow witchers against the Order, Ivar was among them. He fought alongside Arnaghad against his former brothers, and when the posse lost, he left with them. He was a witcher from the School of the Bear after Arnaghad founded it. As the years passed, Ivar focused more on his visions. Realizing he couldn't stop the Wild Hunt alone and that he would get no support from Arnaghad, who believed witchers were only meant to kill monsters for pay, Ivar, along with a group of other witchers, attempted to kill Arnaghad and take over the School. They failed in their attempt, as Arnaghad survived, forcing them to leave the School.[1]

Ivar took his group into the Tir Tochair mountains, where he founded the School of the Viper. He dedicated its purpose to learning as much as possible about the Wild Hunt with the intent of defeating them. To this end, he collected a vast library of books and scrolls on the subject, leading even those witchers from the school who were unaware of its founding purpose to believe that was the true mission of the school.[2]

Although he came to know his enemy extremely well, he was never able to act against them. As he didn't share their means of transportation, he could only watch them. By the time the Wild Hunt was defeated by the witcher Geralt of Rivia, Ivar was long dead.[2]

## _Gwent: The Witcher Card Game_[]

_**Scroll 1:** Ivar founded the Viper School having a great purpose in mind—contrary to rumours that its sole reason for existence was to offer less savoury services. The grandmaster understood that he would not be able to achieve his true goal alone—he intended to find and defeat the Wild Hunt._
    _**Scroll 2:** You see, Ivar was one of the unfortunate few who endured the mutations extremely well, and so was selected for further, more complicated experiments. Of those subjected to these enhancements, only he survived—perhaps due to the mages only managing to partially complete the trial._
    _**Scroll 3:** As a result of these experiments, Ivar gained his moniker, as well as a new sight. His so-called "Evil Eye" saw a different world. Many other worlds, really. With his eye, he watched as ghostly riders dashed along the Spiral, and observed how they'd kidnap, kill, and conquer. Forever haunting Ivar's special vision, these spectres became his obsession._

_**Scroll 4:** Unfortunately, while he managed to get to know his enemy extremely well, he never got close enough to do much about it. Though he could glimpse their rampage from afar, he shared not their mobility, and found himself endlessly chasing shadows. When the Wild Hunt was finally defeated, Ivar was long dead._

_**Chest:** The Witcher School of the Viper made their home in the stronghold of Gorthur Gvaed. Guarded by a remarkable tower adorned by a frighteningly ominous spiral coiled around its contours. Yet it held not a candle to the terrifying moat that surrounded it—deep by several hundred feet and truly... breathtaking. No one could tell if what was filling it should still be called water. The smells above the moat were, to put it mildly, hard to forget. Viper witchers, who survived the fall of the stronghold, later joked that it was the stench that led the Usurper's army to find Gorthur Gvaed. Countless soldiers died in this gutter. According to legends, so many perished that one could have made their way to the other side of the moat on a bridge composed entirely of their corpses. And the odour grew even worse._

### Quick Answers

**What challenges did Kolgrim face returning to the Viper School?**

Kolgrim, a witcher from the Viper School, faced severe challenges when returning. He was wrongly accused of abducting a boy named Vitty, who was actually killed by drowners. This led to a trial by ordeal, where he was tasked with clearing wraiths from White Orchard cemetery. Tragically, Kolgrim was killed by peasants before completing the task, reflecting the distrust and hostility he often faced.

**What was Kolgrim's mission as a witcher of the Viper School?**

Kolgrim, a witcher of the Viper School, was assigned to clear wraiths from the White Orchard cemetery. He was falsely accused of abducting a boy named Vitty, who was killed by drowners. Villagers, acting on this suspicion, killed Kolgrim before he could fulfill his task. 

Provided by: Fandom 

**How was Kolgrim saved from the weeper as a baby?**

As a baby, Kolgrim was rescued by a witcher who killed the weeper that had kidnapped him. The witcher, taking pity on Kolgrim, escorted him back to his mother. Unfortunately, she met them with hatred and disbelief, rejecting the witcher's account. 

Provided by: Fandom 

**What are the lost weapon diagrams Kolgrim sought?**

Provided by: Fandom 

**What are the lost weapon diagrams Kolgrim sought?**

Kolgrim pursued the diagrams for crafting the legendary Viper School witcher gear. These diagrams were essential for creating the renowned Viper School equipment. Kolgrim's quest ended tragically when he died attempting to escape unjust imprisonment for alleged kidnapping. 

Provided by: Fandom 

## Biography[]

As a baby, Kolgrim was abducted on the eve of Saovine by a weeper, who replaced him with its own cursed offspring. However, that same night, a witcher rescued Kolgrim and brought him back to his home. Despite the witcher's explanation and Kolgrim's cries, his mother rejected him, refusing to believe he was her real son. With no other option, the witcher took Kolgrim to the School of the Viper, where he would be raised as one of their own.[1]

Kolgrim's life as a witcher was fraught with hardship, both during his training and throughout his time on the path. 

### White Orchard[]

Kolgrim's life as a witcher was fraught with hardship, both during his training and throughout his time on the path. 

### White Orchard[]

Kolgrim was tasked by the school's founder and master, Ivar Evil-Eye, with finding the Viper School's lost diagrams. After searching the continent, he eventually located them. On his way back to the Viper Keep, Kolgrim stopped in the village of White Orchard in Temeria.

Here, fate once again dealt Kolgrim a cruel hand. While staying near the village, the beekeeper's son, Vitty Smith, went missing, and suspicion quickly fell on Kolgrim. He was arrested, and one of the diagrams was confiscated. Kolgrim was brought before the lord of White Orchard and baronet of Amavet Fortress, Ignatius Verrieres. The lord ordered that Kolgrim be interrogated and tortured when a torturer with the proper qualifications could be found. However, Kolgrim invoked his right to a trial by ordeal. The lord accepted this and tasked him with cleansing his family's crypt of the wraiths that infested it. 

Before Kolgrim could enter the crypt, an enraged mob, led by the boy's father, Paul Smith, overpowered him. The father then beheaded Kolgrim, and the villagers hid his body in the crypt. It was later revealed that Drowners had killed the boy, proving Kolgrim's innocence.

_**Scroll 1:** Fate seemed to take pleasure in torturing Kolgrim. Fortune only smiled upon him if it was accompanied by a stroke of very bad luck. It was always thus, even before Kolgrim became a witcher. When he was still a young harmless brat..._
    _**Scroll 2:** On the eve of Saovine small Kolgrim was kidnapped by a weeper, which replaced him with its own cursed offspring. Fortunately, the monster was slaughtered by a witcher that very same night. The boy's savior, having taken pity on him, decided to escort him back home. Kolgrim was relieved to be returning to the warmth and safety of his mother, unaware of his impending misfortune._

_**Scroll 3:** The woman greeted the witcher with hatred in her eyes, not believing a single word that came out of his mouth. Blinded by her contempt, she refused to even look twice at her own crying son, utterly convinced that the weeper's baby was her real child. With the door slammed shut in their face, the witcher had no other choice than to take Kolgrim with him – straight to the Viper School._
    _**Scroll 4:** Over many future years, fate mocked Kolgrim many times – both during his murderous training and the later travels around the Continent. His life ended most ironically. For he, who was once stolen and then rejected from his mother, was accused of kidnapping a child._
    _**Chest 1:** When master Ivar Evil-Eye instructed Kolgrim to look for the lost weapon diagrams that once belonged to their order, bad luck struck again. Although the witcher managed to find the legendary diagrams, he never returned to their keep.

In the small village of White Orchard, Kolgrim was accused of kidnapping the beekeeper's son. The local baronet, wishing to appease the enraged people, called for a qualified torturer. Justice would be served, no matter what. Their justice, of course, so in response Kolgrim invoked Temerian common law, demanding a trial by ordeal. Surprisingly, the baronet agreed and ordered the witcher to cleanse his family crypt of wraiths.  
According to official sources, Kolgrim perished in the attempt. Yet rumors claimed otherwise. Some locals, enraged by the lordling's decision, supposedly attacked the witcher before he even entered the crypt. The beekeeper had taken his rightful revenge, cutting the mutant's head off with his own hands... Well, 'twas just a rumor. But one thing became clear over time.  
It was drowners that killed the missing boy. Not Kolgrim._

The **"mysterious assassin"** (d. September 1270) was a witcher of the School of the Viper and the first member of the Kingslayers to attempt to kill King Foltest, although he was unsuccessful. Geralt, who was in the process of receiving his reward for destroying Salamandra and eliminating Jacques de Aldersberg, was in the castle when the assassin made his move. A fierce sword fight ensued between the two, narrowly resulting in the assassin's death.

## Biography[]

### Early life[]

## Biography[]

### Early life[]

Since the Viper School is located in the southern part of the Continent, it is possible that he was born somewhere in the Nilfgaardian Empire. At some point during his childhood, he was taken in by the Viper witchers and subjected to the Trials, which mutated him into a being with nearly superhuman speed, strength, and various other abilities.[1] During his training, he became friends with other trainees, including Auckes, Serrit, and Letho.[2]

In the winter of 1269, the foursome helped Geralt of Rivia track down the King of the Wild Hunt after Geralt had saved Letho from a slyzard while on the Path. Together with Geralt, the four Viper witchers fought against the Wild Hunt, until Geralt exchanged himself for Yennefer. Out of respect for their departed comrade, the Vipers took care of Yennefer, who, suffering from amnesia, began to cause trouble for the group. Eventually, they were all captured by the Nilfgaardian secret service. While in custody, they were approached by Imperator Emhyr var Emreis, who offered to rebuild their school if they would sow chaos in the Northern Kingdoms by assassinating its kings.[2]

### Attempt to kill Foltest[]

Critical moment

### Attempt to kill Foltest[]

Critical moment

In September 1270, the assassin managed to infiltrate the Temerian Royal Palace in Vizima, just as Geralt, who had lost his memory shortly after their last encounter, was receiving his reward for destroying Salamandra and killing the Grandmaster of the Order of the Flaming Rose, Jacques de Aldersberg. 

The renegade witcher snuck past all the guards, killing two of them in the process and almost killed King Foltest. Before anything else could happen, Geralt rushed to the king's aid; a hard-fought battle broke out in which the dual-wielding assassin got the upper hand, so Geralt threw his recently-acquired coin pouch at his former comrade to stun him, before cutting off his arm and killing him with a slash across the back. The dead assassin was not recognized by Geralt due to the latter's amnesia, however, and his corpse underwent an autopsy to find out who he was.[3]

She did the autopsy and couldn't identify his age, but did learn that he could see in the dark, indicating to her that he might have been a witcher. The assassin also wore no medallion.

**Serrit** was a witcher of the School of the Viper and a member of the Kingslayers, sent to the Northern Kingdoms by Emperor Emhyr var Emreis to wreak havoc. Along with his brother-in-arms and fellow Viper, Auckes, Serrit was tasked with assassinating King Henselt of Kaedwen.

## Biography[]

Serrit, along with Auckes, Letho and a fourth Viper witcher, met Geralt of Rivia after Geralt saved Letho's life in Angren. As a gesture of thanks, the Viper witchers agreed to help him find the Wild Hunt, who had kidnapped Yennefer. 

During the winter solstice (Midinváerne) of 1270, Serrit took part in the battle of the Hanged Man's Tree, where the witchers faced the riders of the Hunt. Despite their skill, they couldn't defeat all the warriors, resulting in a stalemate. Geralt then offered himself in exchange for Yennefer, and the remaining witchers left with her in tow.

After her return, Yennefer was feverish, delirious, in agony, and suffering from amnesia. Out of respect for Geralt, the witchers took care of her until she recovered. However, Yennefer proved difficult, attempting to seduce Auckes and cause discord among the witchers. This behavior led the group into constant trouble throughout the Nilfgaardian Empire, a kingdom known for its strict rules on mages, which could have resulted in her execution. To protect her, the group wandered through the provinces of the empire, repeatedly rescuing her from various predicaments until they were eventually caught by the imperial secret police.

They were interrogated separately, but no violence was used. After the interrogations, Letho received an offer from Emperor Emhyr var Emreis himself: kill as many northern kings as possible, and in return, the emperor would rebuild the School of the Viper. Letho agreed, recruiting some of his fellow Vipers, including Serrit, to form the group that would become known as the Kingslayers. Like his comrades, Serrit was initially affiliated with Iorveth's band of Scoia'tael, receiving sanctuary from them between assassinations while staying with Iorveth's unit in Upper Aedirn. When Letho returned to them after killing Foltest and attempting to betray Iorveth, the three of them massacred the unit, leaving only one elf alive. They then began plotting Henselt's assassination from their hideout in the gullies.[1]

### Attempt to kill Henselt[]

Serrit was a formidable swordsman, preferring to use two short blades in combat

### Attempt to kill Henselt[]

Serrit was a formidable swordsman, preferring to use two short blades in combat

_If Iorveth's Path was chosen:_ The Kingslayers' hideout was eventually discovered by Síle de Tansarville, leading Dethmold to send Kaedweni soldiers to flush them out. Auckes and Serrit covered Letho's escape but were overwhelmed. One was killed, and the other captured. Under torture, the captured witcher revealed that Letho had gone to Loc Muinne shortly before succumbing to his injuries.[1]

_If Roche's Path was chosen:_ Later, Serrit and Auckes were tasked with assassinating Henselt, the king of Kaedwen. After making their way through the Kaedweni lands, the two witchers set up their hideout in a network of caves near the Kaedweni camp, where they spent their time waiting and planning.

On the day of the strike, they cleared some harpies outside the cave and proceeded to meet with Letho. After a brief conversation about Geralt's presence in the Kaedweni camp and their next move, the witchers set out on their mission. During their walk toward the camp, they discussed the events that were to unfold at Loc Muinne. 

After infiltrating the Kaedweni camp, Serrit secured the palisade while Auckes took care of the ground floor. The witchers met by the cave entrance, where they killed the knights protecting the king. Serrit then entered Henselt's tent and slit the throat of a messenger, only to be confronted by Geralt. Unfazed, Serrit attacked, but Geralt used the sign of Aard to expel him from the tent. Auckes joined Serrit, and the witchers were forced to fight their former companion. While Auckes was cut down by Geralt, Serrit narrowly avoided attacks from Síle's magic and escaped to the Kingslayers' hideout.[1]

## Appearance and personality[]

## Appearance and personality[]

| _Beast or man - makes no difference to me._ |   
---|---|---  
\- _Gwent: The Witcher Card Game_  
  
Serrit was a lot more hot-headed than Auckes, complaining about the lack of action they had in the past days and being anxious to assassinate Henselt, claiming it would be an easy target due to his recklessness. He also didn't seem too troubled by the fact that the king also had a sorcerer and a witcher in his retinue, despite the latter being Geralt. Pragmatic, he cared little about the life of Triss Merigold and Síle and advised that they should be killed to prevent them from revealing their plan.

He seemed to hold Geralt in high regard, thinking of him as a skilled fighter, a friend and a man who could teach him about life in general, this is reflected in the Notes of the kingslayer named Serrit. He also shared an affection for bear traps with Auckes. According to a Scoia'tael prisoner in the Kaedweni camp, Serrit was very proficient in Elder Speech, much more so than Geralt.

## History[]

## History[]

The School of the Bear was founded by the first group of witchers that split off from the Order of Witchers. The witcher Arnaghad had attacked fellow witcher Rhys, nearly killing him. Anticipating that the other witchers would seek to punish him for this, he arrived at the Order's keep with a posse of brothers. After a battle between them and the Order in which the Order subsequently won, Arnaghad and his witchers, including Ivar Evil-Eye, retreated and left the Order.[1] They settled in the Amell Mountains and established contact with the dwarves and gnomes in the region.[2]

Some time after the founding of the school, Ivar wished to dispose of Grandmaster Arnaghad as he knew the witcher wouldn't support trying to take out the Wild Hunt that Ivar saw in his visions, as the grandmaster believed witchers should only be paid to kill monsters. While Ivar and his group almost killed Arnaghad, they ultimately failed to take over and were forced to leave the school. While most of this group went off to found the School of the Viper led by Ivar, another group within this schism led by Iwan split off before the Vipers were founded, eventually creating the School of the Manticore.[1]

At the peak of their power, the Bears often traveled to Skellige, both due to its amount of monsters and the islanders' mindsets being akin to their own.[3] Although the events that led to the establishing of the school happened centuries ago, some of the older witchers from the other schools would refer to them as kinslaying Bears.[1]

The School ceased to function after the Bears failed in a contract to destroy a cabal of vampires. The frustrations of the people in the war-torn provinces around them boiled over into riots. Eventually many of the surrounding villages banded together to destroy the school, as they would rather share the mountains with the monsters than the witchers. The Bear witchers had little to no brotherly bonds with each other and no true loyalty to their school. They decided to part ways with each other and the school, rather than die protecting the keep from the coming humans. Though their keep has been left in disrepair and has been buried by time and the elements, it is believed that some long-time members may have come back to re-occupy it as witchers are necessary again.[2]

## Training[]

## Training[]

Students must pass the trial of the mountain. This requires venturing to the peak of Mount Gorgon to retrieve a special runestone as proof of ascent. It was an especially brutal challenge as many boys freeze to death long before they find the summit. 

## Characteristics[]

Witchers of the Bear School, unlike the Wolves or Griffins, tend to be loners and do not forge strong bonds with their brethren, and so them meeting on the Path can even lead to bloodshed.[3] This is because of the philosophy of the school's founder, who believed that witchers should focus only on the job aspect of their profession. He thought that any code or knightly virtues were just inflated nonsense to feed the ego, and thus favored autonomy above all else. This autonomy extended even to the school itself.[3]

Haern Caduch was a difficult place to live. Due to the cold and snow of the mountains the boys had to huddle up close to the hearthfires or sleep beneath many furs if they didn't they would suffer frostbite or hypothermia. Besides that there was also the never-ending removal of snow from the fortress courtyard. This environment has given the Bear witchers extraordinary endurance even compared to their bretheren from other schools.[3]

They wear heavier armor, favoring defense over agility. Along with the Cat School, they are the only known witcher schools to use crossbows in their hunt.[4] The school may have used shields once. This seems to have been abandoned however after a witcher lost his shield, along with his entire arm.[3]

**Arnaghad** was a witcher from the Order of Witchers and the founder of the School of the Bear. 

## Biography[]

## Biography[]

Arnaghad was a towering figure, both in stature and presence, hailing from the depths of Gemmera. He was known for always wearing a battered bearskin cloak. Despite commanding the respect of many of his fellow witchers, Arnaghad never felt the same sense of kinship that bound the others together. This alienation became starkly apparent when he attacked Rhys, another witcher. 

The incident began when Rhys negotiated a price for slaying a chort that had been terrorizing a highland village in Kaedwen. Arnaghad also arrived in the village, intent on hunting the chort and claiming the reward. When he discovered that another witcher had already taken the contract, Arnaghad's anger flared. He tracked down Rhys in the forest and viciously attacked him, cutting him from shoulder to waist. Rhys narrowly escaped by luring the chort towards Arnaghad, forcing him to fight the monster and allowing Rhys to flee to Morgraig, the Order's keep.

Knowing that the other witchers would seek to punish him for his transgression, Arnaghad arrived at Morgraig with a group of loyal followers. The confrontation quickly escalated into a battle. During the fight, Arnaghad struck fellow witcher Erland of Larvik, wounding him severely across the face. Although the Order ultimately won the battle, it suffered heavy losses. Arnaghad and the surviving members of his posse fled to the Amell mountains, where he established the School of the Bear. There, they crafted bear-shaped medallions to symbolize their new path. 

Years later, Arnaghad was nearly killed in a cruel betrayal that led to the formation of the School of the Viper.[1]

## _Gwent: The Witcher Card Game_[]

_**Scroll 1:** Arnaghad, some would say, was born stubborn. Insolent toward those in authority, he loathed anyone who tried to impose their will upon him, favouring autonomy above all else. This, in large, was the bedrock of why he went on to form his very own witcher school._
    _**Scroll 2:** While other witchers saw in themselves a duty—a purpose that transcended mere necessity⁠—Arnaghad perceived their work as nothing more than that: work. A witcher was to take contracts, kill monsters, and collect coin⁠—anything else, he would argue, was just inflated nonsense to feed the ego._
    _**Scroll 3:** Not wanting to be a slave to a code he did not believe in, he gathered a handful of likeminded witchers and ventured to the Amell mountains, settling into a fortress amid the icy slopes and established the Bear School; a place where would-be witchers could be taught the practicalities of their trade, without the distraction of "honourable virtues" impeding their training._

_**Scroll 4:** Ironically, it was the fundamentals of Arnaghad's school that ultimately led to its dereliction. For the Bear witchers, without sentiment or brotherly comradery to bind them, eventually went their separate ways, seeing no practical reason to stay loyal to each other or the master of their school._

### Quick Answers

**What led Gerd to ally with the usurper in Arcsea?**

Gerd chose to ally with the usurper in Arcsea after turning down Helena Lange-Haare's request to dethrone her father. Despite the usurper's crimes, Gerd supported him and engaged in criminal activities. Helena later deposed her father and issued a warrant for Gerd's arrest, leading him to escape to the Skellige Isles. 

Provided by: Fandom 

**What crimes did Gerd commit while serving the usurper?**

Gerd, a witcher from the School of the Bear, committed crimes such as insulting the heiress, resisting arrest, and collaborating with the usurper. These actions resulted in a warrant for his arrest, with a bounty of 300 Arcsea denars. He later fled to the Skellige Isles. 

Provided by: Fandom

**What is Gerd's connection to the School of the Bear?**

Gerd is linked to the School of the Bear as a witcher. He acted as the loyal guardian to Torgeir the Red, known for repeatedly plundering the City of Golden Towers. 

Provided by: Fandom 

**How did Gerd's behavior insult Helena Lange-Haare?**

Gerd insulted Helena Lange-Haare by rudely rejecting her request to dethrone her father and instead allied with the usurper, committing crimes in his service. Helena responded by issuing a warrant for Gerd's arrest with a bounty of 300 Arcsea denars. 

Provided by: Fandom

Provided by: Fandom 

## Biography[]

### Conflict in Arcsea[]

Provided by: Fandom 

## Biography[]

### Conflict in Arcsea[]

Gerd was summoned to the duchy of Arcsea by Helena Lange-Haare, the heiress to the ducal throne, who sought his help in removing her father from the throne he had unlawfully seized. However, Gerd insulted Helena with his rude behavior and ultimately declined her offer. Despite the atrocities and deaths caused by the usurper, Gerd chose to ally with him, committing various crimes in his service. In a surprising turn of events, Helena successfully overthrew her father and issued a warrant for Gerd's arrest, with a bounty of 300 Arcsea denars.[1] Gerd fled to the Skellige Isles, eventually arriving on the island of Ard Skellig. 

### Time in Skellige[]

### Time in Skellige[]

Upon arriving on Ard Skellig, Gerd encountered locals pleading for help with a dragon that was terrorizing an area near some Elven ruins. Gerd ventured to the ruins and successfully slew the beast, smiling as it drew its last breath.[2] Shortly after, he was contracted by Jorgen Iron Hand to eliminate a siren that had been attacking people in a cave in the northwestern part of Spikeroog. After dealing with the dragon, Gerd sailed to An Skellig and arrived at Fort Tuirseach on the first day of summer, where his appearance brought much joy to all in the castle. He quickly befriended the jarl of An Skellig, Torgeir the Red, after the two shared a barrel of mead. They began hunting together and hosting feasts.

Torgeir soon asked Gerd to rid them of a striga that had made its lair in the ruins of Etnir. Moved by the jarl's plea, Gerd accepted the contract but explained that he first needed to complete his prior commitment to Jorgen Iron Hand. The jarl paid Gerd with a pouch of coins and offered one of his men, Olven, to serve as a guide and, if necessary, a fighting companion. Gerd thanked him and entrusted his prized armor diagrams to the jarl as a promise of his return.[3]

Gerd and Olven sailed to Spikeroog, arriving at the cave infested with sirens. The creatures attacked the men but were swiftly dispatched by Gerd, who used his crossbow to bring them down before finishing them off. After the battle, they made camp in the cave, but by dawn, Olven had died, leaving behind a letter to one Ingeborga Kalebsdotter, admiring the witcher's battle prowess and noting that he had copied Gerd's crossbow diagram.[4]

After completing the contract and taking the siren's head, Gerd returned to a well-known tavern near Fyresdal on Ard Skellig. There, he collected his reward, spent the night drinking, telling tales, and playing gwent with Jorgen and the innkeep. Unfortunately, he lost half his reward and his steel sword diagram to the innkeep in a game of Gwent.[5]

Later that night, a knight from Arcsea, Chalimir, and his men came for Gerd at the inn, setting it ablaze and reducing it to the ruins that remain today. The witcher escaped and made his way to the ruined Fort Etnir to fulfill his contract with the jarl. However, his pursuers caught up with him there. Gerd managed to kill five of them, mortally wound Chalimir, and bring down the fort's roof on them using magic. However, he left behind his silver sword diagram, which his pursuers found after he fled.[6]

Gerd eventually returned to Jarl Torgeir in An Skellig. Shortly thereafter, bandits and Nilfgaardian bounty hunters, paid by the Nilfgaardians, besieged the jarl's castle with catapults. Castle Tuirseach crumbled and fell into ruin, taking with it Jarl Torgeir, his men, and the witcher Gerd.[7]

**Ivo of Belhaven** was a witcher from the School of the Bear, active in the 13th century.

## Biography[]

Ivo was born in Belhaven and, through unknown circumstances, was taken to Haern Caduch to train as a witcher. He did not get along well with his fellow students—one could even say it was hate at first sight—but despite his smaller physique, he managed to hold his own during training. Over time, he became an impressively agile and lethal witcher, bearing more resemblance in style to the Cats or Vipers than to a Bear. After completing his training, he adopted the moniker "of Belhaven" and set off on the Path.

After leaving the school, Ivo distanced himself from other Bear School witchers, remaining indifferent even when he heard the news of Haern Caduch being sacked by peasants. At some point, he crossed paths with the witcher Junod of Belhaven, who, despite sharing the same moniker, was not actually from Belhaven. Just as he had been indifferent about the Bear School's disbandment, Ivo felt nothing upon learning of Junod's death.[1]

### Meeting Meve[]

### Meeting Meve[]

In 1267, during the Second Northern War, Ivo was hired by the Nilfgaardian Empire to kill Gernichora in Ysgith. However, he underestimated her power and was severely injured while fighting off the monsters she sent after him. Ivo eventually joined forces with Queen Meve of Lyria and Rivia and her army, and together they managed to defeat the monsters. After the battle, Ivo explained to Meve what Gernichora was and how to kill her. Impressed by his fighting, Meve offered him a place in her army, but he declined, stating that while he was devoid of emotion, he was not devoid of reason.[2]

Junod of Belhaven was a witcher from the School of the Bear, active in the first half of the 13th century. He met his end in the Owl Eye Grottos beneath the Tufo vineyard in Toussaint while attempting to fulfill a contract. 

## Contents

## Contents

    * 1.1 Becoming a witcher

## Biography[]

### Becoming a witcher[]

Though the origins of Junod were uncertain, he was reputed to be the product of an unusual union between a dwarf and a giantess. Eventually, he became a student at the Bear School, where he trained at Haern Caduch. During his time there, Junod became acquainted with fellow student Ivo from Belhaven. When it came time to choose a sobriquet, Junod adopted "of Belhaven" as his own, despite not being from the town, simply because he liked how it sounded. 

At one point, Junod encountered Ivo on the Path, where Ivo confronted him about the use of the Belhaven name. Junod candidly replied that he liked the ring of it and, given that he didn't expect his smaller colleague to outlive him, felt no qualms about appropriating Ivo's sobriquet.[2]

### Quest for the Grandmaster Gear[]

In 1243, Junod sought out the grandmaster smith Tyen'sail to commission the forging of the Grandmaster Ursine Gear. However, having gambled away all his money, he was in desperate need of work. On May 17th, he accepted a contract from Charité Gontran de Tufo and took the retainer in florens. The following day, he determined that the problems plaguing the vineyard were caused by a subterranean monster, and he decided to venture into the caves the next day. 

As Junod navigated the caves, he drew Bear School emblems on the walls to mark the way out and left a warning for anyone else not to follow him. Unfortunately, he was ill-prepared, lacking crucial knowledge about the monster he was facing. Regretting ever accepting the contract, he confronted the shaelmaar but was ultimately killed in the encounter. No one saw him again.[1]

### Legacy[]

### Legacy[]

A few years after their encounter, Ivo learned of Junod's fate but felt no pity for him.[2] When Geralt of Rivia of the Wolf School visited Toussaint in 1275, he found the diagrams Junod had left behind and succeeded in slaying the Bear School's last foe.[1]

## Appearance and personality[]

| _I remember the bear head medallion that hung from his neck, I remember a towering witcher who haggled like a fishwife._ |   
---|---|---  
\- Lazare Lafargue's impression of Junod, _Blood and Wine_ expansion  
  
As big as a mountain, Junod sported a beard that would put a dwarf elder to shame. His appearence therefore fitted all the stereotypes people had about the Bear witchers. Not being one to hide his thoughts, Junod spoke with refreshing candor.[2]

**Voren of Dillingen** was a witcher from the School of the Bear and the first witcher to test the prosthetic limb designed by the sorcerers Barend Anselberg and Elgan of Verden during the Third Northern War.[1]

## Contents

  * 1 Biography
    * 1.1 Early life
    * 1.2 Second injury
    * 1.3 Life with disability
    * 1.4 Life with prostethic
  * 2 References



## Biography[]

### Early life[]

## Biography[]

### Early life[]

Approximately fifty years before the outbreak of the Third Northern War, Voren was still a relatively inexperienced witcher, having only been on the path for a few years. A fateful hunt south of Cintra would prove to be one of the most significant events of his life. Voren accepted a contract to kill a Fiend that had been terrorizing local villages. Local hunters led him to believe that the Fiend was still a juvenile and could be easily dispatched. Unfortunately, the hunters were mistaken; the Fiend was fully grown. The ensuing battle was long and arduous, but Voren ultimately succeeded in killing the monster. However, one of the Fiend's blows crushed his left arm, shattering the bones in his wrist and fingers.

Having already ingested several witcher potions, Voren decided not to risk drinking a Swallow potion but instead rode to the nearest town, three days away, to seek medical help. By the time he arrived, his witcher healing had already taken effect, fusing the shattered bones together in a twisted manner, making it difficult for him to flex his fingers without great effort. With the help of a splint and time spent adapting, Voren adjusted his fighting style and regained the ability to perform Signs.[1]

### Second injury[]

### Second injury[]

A year after his initial injury, Voren suffered another severe injury to his left arm during a fight with an Ekimmara, which destroyed the splint. Again lacking Swallow, Voren sought medical aid. Unfortunately, by the time he found a doctor, his witcher healing had worsened the situation; the wound had healed, trapping debris from the splint inside his arm, causing a gangrenous infection. The doctor determined that the arm had to be amputated above the elbow. Lacking proper anesthetics and with limited experience in amputations, the procedure was both physically and mentally traumatic for Voren.[1]

### Life with disability[]

### Life with disability[]

A year after the amputation, life was difficult for Voren. Whenever he arrived in towns or villages, contracts were often pulled from the noticeboards, and the work he managed to get was low-paying and required little skill. In the eyes of the commonfolk, he was no longer a capable witcher but a liability. Isolated and impoverished, Voren was reduced to sleeping rough and hunting wild animals to survive in Lyria and Rivia.

At his lowest point, he encountered the mage Elgan of Verden. Elgan, who had lost a leg while hunting a Shaelmaar in Mahakam, offered Voren substantial compensation if he helped in the hunt. Initially reluctant, Voren eventually agreed, reasoning that dying in battle with a monster was better than starving to death. The pair successfully tracked down and killed the Shaelmaar deep in the Dwarven mines. However, as they tried to leave, the tunnel began to collapse, trapping Elgan under debris. Despite the mage's protests, Voren refused to leave him behind and managed to pull him free. The mineshaft collapsed further, burying them both, but with Elgan's magic, they escaped by morning. Grateful for Voren's aid, Elgan later repaid his debt by offering him a new invention: a prosthetic arm designed for a witcher's lifestyle, which Voren would be the first to test in the field.[1]

### Life with prostethic[]

### Life with prostethic[]

Thanks to the prosthetic, Voren was able to perform signs again and take on contracts worthy of a witcher. He was active in Cintra during the Third Northern War and entered into a relationship with a Higher Vampire.[2] Despite his newfound capabilities, the scars of his past injuries remained. Voren continued to suffer from chronic pain, which could flare up and cause phantom limb syndrome where his left arm used to be. The psychological wounds from years of frustration, despondency, and loss also persisted. When not wearing his prosthetic, Voren kept it nearby, having adapted to perform most daily tasks using his right arm alone.[1]

**School of the Manticore** , or **Alqatil** (Zerrikanian: _Slayers_), is a witcher school that was headquartered in the far east,[2] on the edges of the Korath desert. They rarely venture on the other side of the Continent, and thus remain mostly an enigma to Nordlings.[1]

## History[]

## History[]

Around the time the schism happened at the School of the Bear where Ivar Evil-Eye failed to takeover, his group split off and was further joined by others who also didn't share Grandmaster Arnaghad's philosophy, with one of these individuals being Iwan. As this group headed into the Tir Tochair Mountains for a rumored fortress to found the School of the Viper, Iwan realized he also didn't agree with Ivar's view, so as the group headed to the mountains, Iwan and others who also doubted Ivar split off and headed to where they knew they could find work: Elskerdeg Pass in the Tir Tochair Mountains. This pass sat on the edges of the infamous Korath desert where Zerrikanian caravans regularly tried to pass through the treacherous area to trade with the western portion of the continent. In a short time, Iwan and his fellow witchers went from being solely hunters to skilled defenders as they escorted caravans safely back and forth across the desert.[1]

### Golden years[]

### Golden years[]

One day in the desert, Iwan and his group found a royal Zerrikanian caravan under attack by a pair of manticores and ran in to help. After they had killed the monsters, they discovered the caravan was headed to meet mages at Aretuza and among their group was the Zerrikanian Queen's Court Mage, Nasira Faizan. Having seen how skilled the witchers were, Nasira then offered them substantial pay and an audience with the queen if they could get her safely back home to Zerrikania and they readily agreed. Once they got to Zerrikania's capital, the sorceress told all about the "alqatil" exploits and the queen offered a proposal: if the witchers would work exclusively for the crown and guard their merchant caravans and emissaries, then Zerrikania would build a castle on each side of the desert to help build up the school. The witchers agreed and the two castles were built: Behelt Nar in the west and Bialsuf Alsarea in the east, the latter of which Iwan stayed at.[1]

Over the years, Nasira worked with Iwan to recreate the mutation process though Iwan was a bit evasive of giving the full details, having not known the full process himself. They even tried to apply the mutations to some of the famed warrior women of Zerrikania but these experiments were deemed inconclusive. Despite this, they brought in the best warriors to be trained at the new School of the Manticore, with a focus on defense and employing potions. To add to their arsenal they added in special shields made of meteoritic steel and silver. During this time Iwan later changed his name to Imad Asem and became the personal witcher to the Zerrikanian queen.[1]

### Downfall[]


In the fall of 1146, the Queen of Zerrikania organized a royal caravan to arrange a marriage between her son and the Princess of Metinna. As many royal family members and Zerrikanian's court were going, almost the entire school of witchers were called on to protect the caravan across the desert and despite his advanced age, Imad decided to also go. However, what later became known as the Day of Fire happened as the caravan passed within the Fiery Mountains, where the caravan was met by a towering Fire Elemental. Despite having most of the school's witchers there, they didn't have any siege artillery and were unprepared for such a threat. By the time the battle was over, almost all the witchers had been killed along with half of the royal family members and a third of the Zerrikanian court. Due to this, Zerrikania shunned the few remaining witchers and the country turned its focus on finding a safe sea route to the west instead. Having lost the Zerrikanian crown's support, the few witchers that remained fell into decline.[1]

### Later years[]

One of the school's members, Merten, traveled to Toussaint in 1201, seeking the legendary armorer Tyen'sail to order forging of a Grandmaster Gear. Instead, he ended up converting to Lebioda's teachings. Baptized as Shavel, he renounced his witcher past and became a priest.[2]

By 1272, the few Manticore witchers that remained had turned back to monster hunting to make a living and return in the winter to the western fortress, Behelt Nar.[1]

_The Witcher Role-Playing Game_

**Iwan** , later known as **Imad Asem** , was a Witcher originally from the School of the Bear, who eventually went on to found the School of the Manticore. 

## Biography[]

Iwan was originally trained and mutated at the School of the Bear. He never cared much for the school's master, Arnaghad, nor for his brutal teaching philosophies. So when the schism in the Bear School occurred after Ivar Evil-Eye's attempted assassination of Arnaghad, Iwan had no qualms about leaving with the future Vipers as they departed Haern Caduch.

However, the young Witcher soon realized that he did not agree with Ivar's grand ambitions and sense of duty. He also learned of the Witchers' dark prophecy and grim resolutions. As Ivar and his followers moved on in search of Gorthur Gvaed, Iwan and other Witchers who doubted Ivar chose a different path. They headed towards a place where they knew they would find work: the Elskerdeg Pass. This small group of Witchers found ample employment, as merchants hired them to guard their caravans traveling across the Korath Desert. A pivotal event in these days would elevate Iwan and his group to great renown and respect in Zerrikania.

While crossing the desert, Iwan and his fellow Witchers encountered a group of survivors desperately fending off two Manticores. Recognizing the survivors' attire as that of the Zerrikanian royal family, Iwan and his companions swiftly dispatched the monsters. Among the survivors was the court mage, Nasira Faizan. She had heard rumors of foreign warriors protecting merchants traversing the Korath, but witnessing their prowess firsthand left her deeply impressed. Nasira offered Iwan and his comrades their weight in gold and an audience with the Queen if they could safely guide her back to Zerrikania. The Witchers agreed, and upon reaching the capital, they were warmly greeted and introduced to the Queen as "Alqatil," or "Slayers."

After hearing the story of how they saved Nasira, the Queen offered the Witchers an exclusive deal: protect Zerrikania's merchants and emissaries, and in return, they would receive assistance in building their school. Iwan accepted the offer. The school's two castles were built at either end of the Korath Desert, and from then on, they were officially known as the School of the Manticore. 

Iwan assisted Nasira in recreating the mutation process, though he remained vague about the details. He chose to remain in the eastern fortress, Bialsuf Alsarea, with Nasira and the young trainees, eventually becoming the personal Witcher to the Queen of Zerrikania. He also adopted a new name, Imad Asem.

In the autumn of 1146, when the Queen organized a large caravan for her son, the prince, Imad, despite his advanced age, led most of the Manticore Witchers in protecting it. Unfortunately, the caravan met a disastrous end when it was attacked by a colossal Fire Elemental, resulting in the death of most of the Witchers and a large part of the caravan.

### Quick Answers

**What led Merten to seek spiritual enlightenment in Toussaint?**

### Quick Answers

**What led Merten to seek spiritual enlightenment in Toussaint?**

Merten, formerly a witcher from the School of the Manticore, sought spiritual enlightenment in Toussaint around 1203. After years of indulgence, he traveled there in 1201, initially to commission Grandmaster Gear. Instead, he embraced Lebioda's teachings, renouncing his past to become a priest. His transformation involved meditation, prayer, and leaving behind symbols of his former life. Guided by the Great Beggar, Merten visited the Hidden Chapel and experienced a vision at the Lake of Cleansing, marking his spiritual rebirth. 

Provided by: Fandom 

**What is the significance of the Trial of the Grasses for Merten?**

Provided by: Fandom 

**What is the significance of the Trial of the Grasses for Merten?**

The Trial of the Grasses is crucial for Merten, involving a painful process that modifies physiology through special virus cultures and alchemical ingredients. Over about a week, ingredients like corn lily and nightshade, along with mutagenic elixirs, are used to transform individuals into witchers, enhancing their abilities. 

Provided by: Fandom 

**How did Merten's past as a witcher influence his spiritual journey?**

Merten, formerly a witcher from the School of the Manticore, found spiritual enlightenment in Toussaint around 1203. His past, filled with indulgence, led him to seek truth and faith. He abandoned his witcher life, leaving behind symbols of his past, including witcher diagrams, to honor Lebioda. Merten's spiritual journey involved meditation and prayer, culminating in a vision at the Cave of Tribulations, symbolizing his cleansing from past deeds. 

Provided by: Fandom

Provided by: Fandom 

**How did Merten's lifestyle change after joining the School of the Manticore?**

Merten experienced a major lifestyle change after joining the School of the Manticore. Initially known for his indulgence in alcohol and other pleasures, by 1203, he achieved spiritual enlightenment in Toussaint, indicating a move from indulgence to a more spiritual life. 

Provided by: Fandom 

**Why did Merten indulge in pleasures of the flesh during his time on the Path?**

Merten, a witcher from the School of the Manticore, indulged in pleasures of the flesh during his time on the Path. Known for drinking and hedonism, he often engaged in such activities. This behavior led to incidents like arriving drunk at Tyen'sail's workshop and a brawl with the ducal guard, resulting in his arrest and imprisonment at Bastoy Prison Ruins. These actions occurred before his spiritual enlightenment in Toussaint around 1203. 

Provided by: Fandom 

## Biography[]

Provided by: Fandom 

## Biography[]

Like other witchers, Merten was given to the School of the Manticore as a child, where he underwent rigorous training and endured the Trial of the Grasses to become a witcher. 

By 1201, Merten had spent many years on the Path, indulging in all the pleasures of the flesh whenever he could. It came as no surprise, then, when he arrived at the workshop of Tyen'sail completely drunk, seeking to have some grandmaster armor made. The armorer, furious at Merten's state, kicked him out, ordering him to return only if and when he sobered up. Later that day, Merten was arrested for getting into a drunken brawl with the ducal guard and was subsequently locked up in the Bastoy Prison.[1]

While imprisoned, Merten shared a cell with a devout follower of Lebioda, whom he initially mocked and ridiculed. However, around the 30th of Birke, Merten began to have a change of heart. He started asking more about Lebioda's teachings, and over the course of a year, his curiosity grew into genuine interest. Upon his release, Merten set off on a new Path, determined to leave his old life behind. His first stop on Lebioda's pilgrimage was a cave where the prophet had once received enlightenment.[2] Within the cave, Merten vowed to atone for his sins, leaving behind a prayer inscribed on the back of a diagram, asking Lebioda for strength to complete the pilgrimage. His next destination was the Temple of Lebioda, where he sought the guidance of the Great Beggar.[3]

Merten arrived at the temple around 14 Feainn 1203, where he conversed at length with the Great Beggar before confessing his sins. The Great Beggar then informed Merten that if he truly wished to cleanse himself of his past deeds, he would need to journey to the Hidden Chapel. Before departing, Merten left behind additional witcher diagrams, symbolizing his detachment from his former life.[4]

A few days later, Merten arrived at the Cave of Tribulations. After successfully enduring the cave's trials, he meditated and experienced a vision of a crystal-clear lake, the Lake of Cleansing. Before departing for his final destination, he left yet another diagram behind.[5] On 32 Feainn 1203, Merten reached the lake, where he wrote a letter reflecting on his journey. He then cast the letter, along with his final attachments to his old life, into the lake. Renouncing his life as a witcher, Merten rechristened himself as Shavel and vowed to spread Lebioda's wisdom throughout the world, starting in the North and eventually reaching as far as the Dragon Mountains.[6]

**School of the Crane** is a witcher school established after the Second Conjunction, somewhere in the lands of Eastern Coast of the Western Continent or the adjacent seas. 

## Characteristics[]

Skilled in both swords and early guns, the Cranes prove to be the best remedy to monsters of the air and the sea which can be encountered on long routes between Cherdian and Novigrad.

While expecting to fight a sea monster, a witcher of this School prepares a long rope, one end of which they binds to the mast of a vessel and the other to a close-fitting protective suit covering their whole body except for hands, feet and the head. When not expecting to fight such, they prefer to wear no significant armor, just belts for swords and guns.[1]

## Notes[]

Crane School Putnam by Yama Orce

## Notes[]

Crane School Putnam by Yama Orce

  * The school first appeared in Volodymyr Arenev's short story _Wesoły, niewinny i bez serca_ ("Cheerfull, Innocent, and Heartless") for _Tales from the world of The Witcher_ , a Witcher short-story collection by Ukrainian and Russian writers. It was later mentioned in _The Witcher: Old World_ as an easter-egg.
  * While the School doesn't belong to CD PROJEKT RED's The Witcher franchise as of this moment (the Old World appearance was an easter-egg), CD PROJEKT RED's lead concept artist Yamandu Orce, in consultation with other developers, has drawn an art of Witcher190/Piemsito's fan character Putnam Pitch, the School's fanfic founder. This doesn't mean that the character is canon (the artwork was commissioned) but the drawing itself is probably the closest to how CDPR would imagine the School's equipment.

### Quick Answers

### Quick Answers

**Who was Madoc's mentor during his witcher training?**

Provided by: Fandom 

**What role did Madoc play in the Order of Witchers?**

Madoc, a witcher from the Order of Witchers, was among the first to endure the mutation process. He possessed superhuman abilities, excelled in swordsmanship and alchemy, and utilized signs. 

Provided by: Fandom 

**How did nobles influence Madoc's training as a witcher?**

Madoc, a witcher from the Order of Witchers, underwent the Trials, a series of grueling tests including sword skill, monster lore, and rudimentary spells. These were administered by renegade mages like Alzur in the 10th century. The painful process, often fatal, gave Madoc superhuman abilities, swordsmanship, and alchemical skills. 

Provided by: Fandom

Provided by: Fandom 

**How did Madoc survive the witcher mutation process?**

Madoc survived the witcher mutation process as one of the first from the Order of Witchers. This process, called the Trial of the Grasses, involves dangerous mutations that grant witchers superhuman abilities. Madoc's survival suggests a high tolerance to these mutations, which are crucial for skills in swordsmanship, alchemy, and magical signs. 

Provided by: Fandom 

**What challenges did Madoc face as a child witcher?**

Madoc, from the Order of Witchers, faced severe challenges as a child witcher. He survived the early mutation process, which included the Trials. These trials were grueling, involving sword skills, monster lore, herbalism, and Signs. The process was painful and often deadly, using mutagens, magic, and alchemy. Despite these hardships, Madoc emerged with superhuman abilities. 

Provided by: Fandom 

## Biography[]

Provided by: Fandom 

## Biography[]

As a child, Madoc was either taken from the streets or sold by his parents to the mage Alzur, who brought him to Morgraig to undergo training as a witcher. The mages, including Alzur, Cosimo Malaspina, and Idarran of Ulivo, treated Madoc and the other children coldly, only showing emotion during visits from the nobles or kings who funded the creation of witchers. Despite the hardships, Madoc formed bonds with the other children, but many of them perished due to the mutations and trials they were subjected to. Madoc and the surviving children were often left to bury their dead friends themselves. Despite the immense challenges, Madoc endured and became one of the first witchers. 

Madoc's time at the Order of Witchers was brief, as he left the order and Alzur behind, consumed by bitterness, resentment, and guilt over surviving when so many others had not. He eventually found work as a bodyguard for a merchant traveling from Vizima to Maribor.

The merchant traveled as part of a group consisting of two dwarves, a soldier, a Halfling, and the retired bard Galanthea. One night, while the group made camp, Galanthea began telling the story of how she met Alzur and how he had saved her. Madoc, skeptical that Alzur would do anything out of kindness, only grunted or spat when addressed by the others. When the topic of witchers came up, he feigned ignorance before going on a patrol of the area. During the night, the camp was attacked by a Wererat, which killed the merchant and one of the dwarves. Madoc engaged the monster as it charged toward Galanthea. He managed to bring the creature to its knees, but it grabbed him by the throat as it quickly regenerated. Acting swiftly, Madoc cast Igni at the wererat, melting its head, and then dropped a bomb at the creature's feet, killing it.

As the caravan resumed its journey, Madoc spoke with Galanthea, revealing what Alzur had done to him and the other children, insisting that Alzur cared only about his ego and legacy, not about making a better world. Galanthea, however, thanked him for saving them and expressed her gratitude for his presence. Madoc nodded and moved ahead to ensure they wouldn't run into any further trouble.

Later, when he returned to the group, he found their cart abandoned near an inn, with blood on the ground. Approaching a peasant standing guard outside, Madoc punched him in the stomach when he was told to leave and entered the inn. Inside, he found a group of peasants pilfering through the belongings of his travel companions. The leader of the group, a woman, aimed a crossbow at him and threatened to shoot if he didn't leave. When Madoc's attempts to calm her down failed, she fired the arrow, but Madoc deflected it with his sword, causing it to strike another peasant in the throat. The entire group then surrendered, and Madoc ordered them to leave.

After freeing his companions, Madoc dug a grave for the peasant he had inadvertently killed. While digging, Galanthea approached him, revealing that she knew his name because Alzur had spoken of him. She claimed that Alzur had been fond of Madoc. Initially angered by this, Madoc listened as Galanthea urged him to let go of his resentment and live life for himself. As Madoc prepared to resume digging, it began to rain. He watched, amused, as his companions and the innkeeper frantically collected rainwater. However, his amusement turned to concern when he noticed clouds gathering over Maribor and a portal opening in them. The group watched in horror as a giant monster, the Viy of Maribor, emerged. Without hesitation, Madoc jumped on his horse, looked back at the group one last time, and rode off to face his fate.

**Rhys** was a witcher from the Order of Witchers.[1]

## Biography[]

One day, Rhys accepted a contract to hunt down a chort that had been terrorizing a highland village in Kaedwen. While tracking the monster deep within the nearby forest, he was confronted by a fellow witcher, Arnaghad.

Arnaghad, who had also been after the same contract, became enraged upon discovering that another witcher had beaten him to it. Determined to confront the one who had outpaced him, Arnaghad found Rhys and attacked him, slashing him from shoulder to waist. Despite his injuries, Rhys managed to escape by drawing the chort's attention towards them. As the monster charged, Rhys used the distraction to slip away into the wilderness. 

Fortunately, Rhys survived the attack by quickly consuming a swallow potion, which aided in his recovery. He then made his way back to the Order's seat at Morgraig castle to inform the other witchers of the incident.

## Biography[]

### Early Life[]

Adela was traveling with her mother and several other families. One day, they were approached by a group of witchers under the command of Gwidon. The group surrounded the caravan and, upon Gwidon's signal, killed all the adults and abducted the children. During the attack, Adela was wounded. 

She was found by Geralt, who had witnessed the attack during his trial in the forest. He nursed her back to health. When she regained consciousness, she recognized the necklace Geralt was wearing as her mother's. Geralt commented that he had found it on the road. Realizing what that meant, Geralt comforted her and told her to be brave.

When the Old Witcher came to pick up Geralt after the trial's end, the children told him what had happened. They were then brought to Kaer Morhen, where they testified to the witcher council about the attack and were present when Gwidon and his group were banished. 

### Life as Witcher[]

Unlike Geralt, Adela did not remain at the Wolf School. She went to a witcher school beyond the mountains, where she underwent training. 

One day, she returned to Kaer Morhen with two of her fellow witchers. On their way, they came across Geralt, Clovis, and Gascaden, who were nearly fighting after Gascaden had made a remark to Clovis. Upon approaching them, Adela greeted the group and remarked that they were drinking potions without an instructor present, warning them to be careful. 

As she began to leave, Geralt asked for her name and said he had seen her before, to which Adela replied that he had not.

As she began to leave, Geralt asked for her name and said he had seen her before, to which Adela replied that he had not. 

Sometime later, she was swimming in a lake when Geralt approached her. She asked what the matter was and if he recognized her, as he had claimed before. When he said he was mistaken, she agreed, asking how he could possibly know women. She then said she would now watch as he swam. 

When Geralt began undressing, she asked if he was truly a witcher, since witchers were supposed to be asexual—something he clearly was not. When he replied that he didn't know, she grabbed her things and left. 

A training duel was later organized between Adela and her fellow witchers against Geralt and Clovis. Adela chose to duel Geralt. During the duel, Geralt mostly used evasive maneuvers and even disarmed her, earning a reprimand from Sorel. When Geralt re-engaged in the duel, he let Adela win.

She was present when Geralt, Gascaden, and Clovis began their punishment, and also when the witcher council informed Geralt that he had been found not guilty of the charges brought against him. 

While Geralt was training in the woods under the watch of the Old Witcher, Adela sought him out and asked if he wanted to train with her, as she was also leaving on a mission—but Geralt couldn't. 

She approached Geralt again, this time while he was alone. She measured his pulse, thinking he was in a trance, and was surprised by how high his heartbeat was. Concluding she had surprised him, she asked if he had been thinking about her. 

Geralt asked how she knew and when she would be leaving. As she was departing soon, he asked if she could teach him how to control his heartbeat. She had him place his hand on her chest to feel her own heartbeat.

They met up again later and were intimate. Afterward, she informed Geralt she was leaving the next day. When Geralt asked her to stay, she became upset, saying they would never meet again and that he wasn't a real witcher. 

As he tried to approach her, she drew her sword and told him to leave, calling him a nobody. As he left, she thrust her sword into the ground in frustration. 

She then reported to Sorel but said nothing—only nodded. When Sorel asked if she would testify before the council and if Geralt was a man, she shook her head. This made Sorel angry, and he told her to leave. She then rode off from Kaer Morhen, smiling one last time at Geralt.

## _The Hexer_

  * English cover 
  * Polish movie poster 



_**The Hexer**_ (Polish: _Wiedźmin_) is the international title of both a movie (2001) and a television series (2002) based on the witcher short stories by Andrzej Sapkowski, although it is more commonly referred to as _**The Witcher**_ by fans since the release of _The Witcher_. Both the movie and the television series were directed by Marek Brodzki, written by Michał Szczerbic, and produced by Lew Rywin. The role of Geralt was played by Michał Żebrowski, and the music was composed by Grzegorz Ciechowski. 

The theatrical movie was essentially the then-unreleased TV series chopped into about 2 hours, and received very poor reviews from both fans and critics. The 13-episode TV series came out the following year. The series was much more coherent than the confusing movie, but was still considered a failure mostly due to the film's already bad reputation and due to vast changes to the source material.

**Danusia Stok** is the translator of _The Last Wish_ by Andrzej Sapkowski from Polish into English. She also translated _Blood of Elves_ , however starting with _Time of Contempt_ , the novels have instead been translated by David French. Aside from _The Witcher_ series, she translated the motion picture play for the Three Colors Trilogy and several English and Polish language textbooks.

There have been three series of **comic books** based on Andrzej Sapkowski's _The Witcher_ series. A series published in Poland between 1993 and 1995, a 2011 miniseries published by Egmont, and the currently ongoing series published by Dark Horse Comics, started in 2014. The latter two series are part of CD PROJEKT RED's _The Witcher_ franchise.

## Parowski/Polch series[]

Wiedźmin cover

From 1993-1995, 6 issues of _The Witcher_ comic books, based on Andrzej Sapkowski's Witcher short stories, was published in Poland. They were written by Maciej Parowski and illustrated by Bogusław Polch. 

The original issues were (in order of publication):

The original issues were (in order of publication): 

  1. _Droga bez powrotu_ (_A Road with No Return_ , based on the short story _Droga, z której się nie wraca_)
  2. _Geralt_ comic (based on the short story "The Witcher")
  3. _Mniejsze zło_ (based on the short story "The Lesser Evil")
  4. _Ostatnie życzenie_ (based on the short story "The Last Wish")
  5. _Granica możliwości_ (based on a short story "The Bounds of Reason")
  6. _Zdrada_ (_The Betrayal_ , not based on a short story, but on an outline by Andrzej Sapkowski)



In 2001, the graphic novels were collected in 2 hardcover volumes, in the order of internal chronology: 

### Volume 1[]

  1. _Droga bez powrotu_
  2. _Zdrada_
  3. _Geralt_



### Volume 2[]

  1. _Mniejsze zło_
  2. _Ostatnie życzenie_
  3. _Granica możliwości_



In 2025, these comics were released in English by Dark Horse as a single volume titled _The Witcher: Classic Collection._

## CD PROJEKT RED's _The Witcher_ franchise[]

## CD PROJEKT RED's _The Witcher_ franchise[]

Since 2011, new _Witcher_ comics are being released as part of CD PROJEKT RED's franchise. The depiction of Geralt and other characters in these comics are based on _The Witcher 2: Assassins of Kings_ and _The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt_ video games and are authorized by CD PROJEKT RED. They are not in any way related to the previous Parowski/Polch series. 

### Egmont series[]

Geralt in Racja stanu

In 2011, Egmont released a 2-part comic book not based on any of the novels or short stories (instead containing a new adventure for Geralt). It was written by Michał Gałek, illustrated by Arkadiusz Klimek, and colorized by Łukasz Poller. 

  * _Reasons of State_



### Standalone[]

Late on in 2015, a separate comic was released by CD PROJEKT RED that expanded on CD PROJEKT RED's storyline after the events in the second game. 

  * _Matters of Conscience_



### Dark Horse series[]

* _Matters of Conscience_



### Dark Horse series[]

Dark Horse Comics released four sets of comic series in 2014 to 2016 made up of 4 comics written by Paul Tobin and illustrated by Joe Querio. While the first storyline, _House of Glass_ , is an original story, the second one, _Fox Children_ , is an adaptation of one of the chapters of Andrzej Sapkowski's _Season of Storms_ novel. 

  * _House of Glass_
  * _Fox Children_
  * _Killing Monsters_ (standalone)
  * _Curse of Crows_

**Tales of magic and monsters as told by The World's Greatest Bard!**

Adventure across the world of _The Witcher_ , uncovering its secrets, slaying its monsters, and bringing its stories to life, as entirely and truthfully recollected by the famed bard Dandelion. In this book, you'll travel from the could mountains of Kovir to the wine soaked region of Toussaint in Nilfgaard, meeting interesting characters along the way, with intrigue around every corner. _**Book of Tales**_ is a supplement for _**The Witcher Pen and Paper RPG**_ that gives you six adventures that span the Continent, complete with new monsters, player content, and maps. All compiled into a larger campaign. 

**Featuring...**

**Featuring...**

  * **Six Adventures** : Experience escapades across the Continent, including a murder mystery in the heart of Mount Carbon, pulse-pounding combat in the Claremont Arena, and investigations in the mist-shrouded Alderwood.
  * **New Player Content** : Expand your game with new weapons, new spells, and three new playable races: Gnomes, Vran, and Werebbubbs.
  * **A Connected Campaign** : Take your party on a journey across the Continent by weaving all six adventures into a country-hopping trek.

**Geralt of Rivia** (b. 1160) was a witcher who was tied to Ciri through the Law of Surprise. While initially reluctant to accept his destiny, Geralt eventually came to terms with his fate. Despite their tumultuous relationship, he also loved the sorceress Yennefer of Vengerberg.

### Quick Answers

**What is the Law of Surprise that ties Geralt to Ciri in the Netflix series?**

In the Netflix series 'The Witcher', the Law of Surprise is a custom as old as humanity itself. It dictates that a man saved by another is expected to offer his savior a boon whose nature is unknown to one or both parties. Geralt invoked the Law of Surprise on Duny just before Pavetta threw up, revealing to everyone she was pregnant with Ciri and therefore Ciri would become Geralt's Child of Surprise. This would highlight the destiny of the relationship between Geralt and Ciri in the series. 

Provided by: Community 

**Who is Yennefer of Vengerberg to Geralt of Rivia in the Witcher Netflix series?**

Provided by: Community 

**Who is Yennefer of Vengerberg to Geralt of Rivia in the Witcher Netflix series?**

In the Witcher Netflix series, Yennefer of Vengerberg is a significant character in Geralt of Rivia's life. She is Geralt's love interest and also plays a crucial role as a teacher and adoptive mother to Ciri. Yennefer and Geralt share a deep bond, often stepping out together for various events and adventures. Their relationship is complex and layered, often described as being destined for each other, yet needing something more than destiny alone to sustain it. 

Provided by: Fandom 

**What is the significance of the town of Blaviken to Geralt in the Witcher series?**

Provided by: Fandom 

**What is the significance of the town of Blaviken to Geralt in the Witcher series?**

Blaviken holds a significant place in Geralt's story in the Witcher series. It was in this town that Geralt earned one of his infamous monikers, the 'Butcher of Blaviken'. This title was given to him after a series of fateful events involving him, Renfri, and her gang. Geralt was passing through Blaviken during its busiest market event when he got entangled in a conflict between Renfri, an ousted princess, and the local mage, Stregobor. Both parties tried to get Geralt to side with them, leading to a violent confrontation that earned Geralt his nickname. 

Provided by: Fandom 

**Who is Renfri and how does she relate to Geralt in the Witcher Netflix series?**

Provided by: Fandom 

**Who is Renfri and how does she relate to Geralt in the Witcher Netflix series?**

Renfri, portrayed by Emma Appleton in the Witcher Netflix series, is a princess and the daughter of Fredefalk, the prince of Creyden. She is also known by the alias 'Shrike'. Renfri is a skilled swordsman and has a bandit profession. Her life takes a dramatic turn when Stregobor attempts to have her assassinated, leading her to swear vengeance on him. Her path crosses with Geralt of Rivia, our main character, resulting in a fatal encounter. Geralt is forced to kill Renfri, marking a significant event in the series. 

Provided by: Fandom 

**What is the backstory of Geralt of Rivia in the Witcher Netflix series?**

Provided by: Fandom 

**What is the backstory of Geralt of Rivia in the Witcher Netflix series?**

In the Witcher Netflix series, Geralt of Rivia is a Witcher hailing from the Wolf School. Born in 1160, Geralt underwent a mutation that granted him superhuman abilities, including exceptional swordsmanship and the ability to use alchemy and signs. His hair, originally brown, turned milk-white as a result of the mutation, earning him the White Wolf moniker. Throughout the series, Geralt uses his skills to navigate the complex and often dangerous world of the Continent. 

Provided by: Community 

## Biography[]

### Early life[]

Provided by: Community 

## Biography[]

### Early life[]

As a child, Geralt was raised by his mother Visenna, unaware that he would one day be handed over to the witchers to be trained as one of them. Around 1165, while still young, the fated day came when Visenna left him in the mountains of Kaedwen and the witcher Vesemir picked him up. Geralt was then taken to Kaer Morhen to be trained, alongside Eskel, Lambert, and Remus. He survived the Trial of the Grasses and underwent the transformation involved in becoming a witcher, and in the process, his hair turned white. 

### Meeting Princess Renfri[]


In 1231, Geralt of Rivia, now a well-known witcher, went to Blaviken in search of an alderman who he hoped would pay him for having killed a kikimora in the nearby swamp. In the village, he met Renfri in a tavern, where he was met with hostility from the other patrons, as they don't want people of his class there. He then met Marilka, the daughter of the alderman. While Marilka assured him that the alderman would not pay him for the kikimora, she directed him to a sorcerer named Stregobor, who had lured Geralt into town to hire him to assassinate Renfri. Stregobor explained his reasoning behind wanting to kill Renfri: the Curse of the Black Sun. This solar eclipse marked the imminent return of the goddess Lilit, whose sole purpose was to exterminate the human race. Stregobor had studied the girls born around the Black Sun in the past and found that they had all been mutated by the eclipse. He had tried to cure them, locking them in towers for safekeeping, but each girl had died. He now believed eliminating them was the lesser evil. 


Renfri, princess of Creyden and daughter of Fredefalk, was one of the girls in Blaviken hunting Stregobor because he had targeted her. He had personally delivered Renfri under the Black Sun and had been given evidence of how the curse had affected her (including killing animals and maiming her maid); he therefore knew for certain that she was the bringer of evil. Previously, in fear of Lilit's return, Stregobor had dispatched someone to follow Renfri into the woods. The man was later found in the brush with Renfri's broach jammed in his ear. She had then disappeared shortly thereafter, hadn't reappeared for another two years, and began chasing Stregobor, plotting her revenge. Stregobor told Geralt that he would stop her himself, except for the fact that she was resistant to magic given her mutation, which Geralt was skeptical of. Geralt refused Stregobor's offer to pay him for killing Renfri because he only kills monsters. When Stregobor asked Geralt to do it anyway because killing Renfri would be the lesser evil compared to letting her harm people, he continued to refuse, because either choice he could make would still be an evil in the end. 

Renfri, the woman from the tavern, tracked Geralt down outside Blaviken and inquired about Geralt's meeting with Stregobor, admitting that she wanted to kill him for the injustices she had suffered; Stregobor's man, who followed her into the woods, had raped and robbed her before letting her go, and she blamed Stregobor for stealing her life as a princess from her. She attempted to recruit Geralt's help in killing Stregobor. Still, Geralt responded by insisting that if Renfri killed Stregobor, she would only be confirming Stregobor's accusations of her being a monster, which he knew from his own experience. Geralt advised Renfri to leave Blaviken and Stregobor behind for a new life for herself.

Renfri followed Geralt back to his camp, where he was recounting his first monster kill to Roach, his mare. The "monster" in question was a man whom Geralt had encountered trying to rape a girl, and after Geralt killed him, the girl who was drenched in the man's blood, was afraid of him. That that had been the day he realized the world didn't need him and that he would only ever be seen as a monster. Renfri came forward and questioned what Geralt believes in, as it was neither destiny nor choosing the lesser evil. Geralt answered that he simply kills monsters; he doesn't take sides. Renfri told him that she'd decided to leave Blaviken for good the next day, based on what Geralt had said about continuing her quest for revenge, making her a monster. When Renfri confirmed that Geralt understood her better than anyone had in a long time, the connection that had been forming between them since they met in the tavern came to a head, and they kissed and then had sex.

After, while dreaming of his night with Renfri, Geralt heard her tell him of his future: he would be run out of Blaviken with thrown stones, tormented by the choice he would make, and the "girl in the woods" is his destiny, one which he could not escape. Geralt awakened alone in the woods of Blaviken, realizing that Renfri had lied about leaving.


He went into town to stop her, where he was met by Renfri's soldiers, men whom she had recruited while hunting Stregobor. He dispatched them with ease. He then found Renfri holding a blade to Marilka's throat, and she threatened to kill her and everyone in Blaviken until Stregobor came down from his tower to face her. Geralt warned her one last time to leave Blaviken, using a display of magic to threaten her further. However, Stregobor was right about magic not affecting Renfri—only silver would have one, as with monsters. Renfri released Marilka and attacked Geralt, who forced himself to fight, managing to cut him several times before Geralt disarmed her and left her with only a dagger to combat him. Geralt then lowered his sword, presenting her with an opportunity to attack or disengage with him. As she chose to lunge at him, he evaded her attack and stabbed her in the throat with her own dagger. As Renfri bled out in Geralt's arms, she repeated that the "girl in the woods" would be with him always, echoing what was said in his dream, and commented on how similar they were to one another. 

Stregobor came down to see the destruction left in Renfri and Geralt's wake, and he ordered Marilka to bring him a cart so that they could take her back to the tower for an autopsy. When Geralt objected, Stregobor informed him that Renfri's mutation enabled her to influence her followers and that he therefore wanted to study her body.
