He asked if she liked his eyes and if she knew what they did to witchers to improve their eyes. It didn't always work. Only three out of ten boys survived the trial to become a witcher. He questioned if his mother knew this when she gave him up to Vesemir. She told him not to ask any more questions as the answers would only hurt them both. Instead, she urged Geralt to find Princess Cirilla. Geralt awakened from his sleep, asking Yurga where the woman had gone, but she was never actually there. He then asked how far Yurga's house is from Sodden, to which he replied an hour on a swift enough horse. Geralt hopped on the back of Yurga's carriage, headed for Sodden. While Yurga can't repay Geralt for saving his life, he can offer him the Law of Surprise. 

Yurga arrived home with Geralt on his back, in a carriage. Zola, his wife, told Yurga that she met an orphan girl in the nearby woods. Hearing Yurga's conversation with his wife reminded Geralt of what Renfri told him all those years ago: the "girl in the woods" is his destiny. Geralt jumped off the back of the carriage and into the woods, where he met Ciri for the first time, as she ran into his arms. "People linked by destiny will always find each other", that Geralt repeats what his mother told him. Ciri then asked who Yennefer was.[8]

### Lifting Nivellen's Curse[]


Taking place in late 1263 and early 1264, after meeting Ciri in the woods, Geralt traveled with her to the site of the Battle of Sodden Hill in search of Yennefer. They crossed paths with Tissaia de Vries and from her Geralt learned that they'd won the battle thanks to Yennefer. Upon understanding that she'd possibly died, Geralt took Tissaia's response as an acknowledgment of Yennefer's death. He asked if winning the war was worth Yennefer's life. Geralt held back tears as he walked back towards Ciri. She continued to wonder who Yennefer is, but Geralt said it didn't matter anymore; she's gone. Geralt and Ciri continued their journey. Resting, Ciri tried to get some sleep, but couldn't. Geralt told Ciri that he couldn't sleep either. Changing the subject, Ciri asked about the Law of Surprise, and Geralt explained that it was from saving her father's life from her grandmother, which earned him the Law of Surprise, which he had obviously invoked jokingly, and which ultimately earned him her, but without expecting it. Second, his later invocation on merchant Yurga which once again connected him to Ciri. 

As night fell, Geralt and Ciri continued riding through a woods, eventually stumbling upon an abandoned village. Geralt is quite confused about it because it is empty there is no one there. Geralt knew somewhere nearby, and he and Ciri sought refuge with an old friend of his, Nivellen, who they discovered had been cursed by a priestess and turned into a beast after trashing the Temple of the Lionheaded Spider while high on godflesh mushrooms, condemned to live alone forever. He let Geralt and Ciri take refuge in his house. The mansion operates under magical control, and Nivellen magically summoned a hot bath for Ciri while taking Geralt out for a beer. After the bath, Ciri joined Nivellen and Geralt. Nivellen called a banquet and told Ciri how he and Geralt met.

Geralt and Nivellen had met many years ago, when Nivellen's father hired Geralt to get rid of a wyvern infestation. Nivellen tried to prove himself to his father by killing one first, but instead fell into their lair. Luckily, Geralt saved him and slayed the wyvern. He then handed Nivellen the wyvern's head and told his father that Nivellen was the one who'd killed it. Speaking about the cause of Nivellen's curse, Geralt knows that curses can be cured by asking Nivellen what the priestess told him. Nivellen replied that she shouted something about "Blood and Love," but he didn't remember exactly.


After dinner, Geralt wondered about the village at the foot of the abandoned hill. Nivellen replied that deserters and thieves roamed the countryside in search of loot. The townspeople decided to leave to save themselves after the Battle of Sodden. Geralt was not convinced that the Battle of Sodden would cause an entire town to leave its home. Nivellen told him it was because of the Wild Hunt. Ciri knew them as the Wraiths of Mörhogg; her grandfather saw them before the fall of Cintra, but Geralt said his grandfather was just a drunk. Geralt was still not convinced, so Nivellen told him that the end of days might be at hand. He responded that he had gone through the Dark Ages, as well as three supposed end-of-days. He told Nivellen that the end of days was nothing but bullshit. Hearing scratching noises from above, Nivellen assured them that is his cat, Vereena. However, Geralt is skeptical and wanted to investigate. While outside with Roach, Geralt noticed footprints in the snow outside the estate, and after a few steps, they disappeared. 


Suspecting Nivellen was hiding something, Geralt challenged him to a drinking game, hoping to get some answers. They threw daggers at a portrait of Nivellen's father, and whoever missed had to drink and tell the truth. Unfortunately for Geralt, he missed every throw, whereas Nivellen had near-perfect aim and asked what had changed Geralt after willingly spending many lifetimes alone. Geralt replied that it was not what but who, Yennefer, who unfortunately died, as far as he was aware. Nivellen was intrigued that someone like Yennefer could win the heart of a witcher. After, Nivellen wonders if Geralt told Ciri the truth about how witchers obtain children so they can feed them with magic herbs. The few who survive become witchers themselves, and all human feelings and reactions are trained out of them, turning them into monsters to kill other monsters. However, Geralt insists it won't come to that. Geralt then pulled his own knife from his boot and hit the portrait spot on, uncovering the fact that Nivellen was cheating with magic knives, leading Geralt to question what he was hiding. But he avoided the questions and wented to relieve himself. 

Geralt checked Nivellen to see if he was asleep. Then he went to the town below to investigate. Immediately, inside he saw frozen corpses. Geralt drew his sword and prepared for the worst. Geralt investigated the corpses and found bloody footprints. The footprints stopped and left only a few drops of blood before disappearing. Geralt indicated that the monster responsible was a winged creature called a bruxa.

Upon discovering that Vereena is the bruxa, who was there in the house, Geralt awoke Ciri and warned her to run. Takes an elixir to prepare himself and followed the sounds bruxa's purring to Nivellen's room, finds Vereena draining and feeding his blood from him. A fight ensued, which eventually led outside, where Vereena takes Ciri hostage but Nivellen impales her. Geralt then managed to wound her before beheading her and it breaks Nivellen's curse which is cured by having his true love taken from him. It was then that not only was Nivellen's curse broken due to the death of his true love, but that he revealed the real reason behind his curse: he raped the priestess, a truth he hid until the end. The ugly revelation left Geralt and Ciri somewhat disgusted. Geralt decided to remain silent and leave with Ciri. Nivellen begged Geralt to kill him, but Geralt said he could kill himself since he became mortal again.

In the woods, after the elixir wore off, Geralt harshly reminded Ciri for disobeying his orders earlier. He told her that she should do what he says the next time they get into trouble. Ciri told Geralt that she understood and would not disobey him again. Ciri then said that everywhere she went people died, that sometimes she felt like she could burn the entire world to the ground even if she didn't want to. His destructive feelings generated great fear in him. Geralt replied that fear was a disease. If left untreated, it could consume anyone. He promised Ciri he won't let anything happen to her.[9]

### Returning to Kaer Morhen[]

### Returning to Kaer Morhen[]

Geralt and Ciri arrived at Kaer Morhen, where he reunited with his witcher brethren and his mentor and father figure Vesemir. While everyone celebrated, the witcher Lambert told a story about a job he once had. When Eskel arrives, boasting after a six-hour fight against a leshy. He brought the monster's hand as proof. Eskel told everyone that he could have ended the fight sooner, but he had lost all of his elixirs. Geralt was confused, as it had been a while since a leshy had been seen. Vesemir questioned his story and asked him whether he didn't think about the leshy's weakness: burning his heart. The other witchers, including Geralt, also began to hesitate before Eskel directed his attention to Ciri.

Trained outside, Geralt was lightly scolded by Vesemir for claiming his Child Surprise and bringing her within their walls. He told him that adopting the Law of Surprise was a big mistake. Previously, Geralt had told Vesemir that he would not take the girl. However, he had to save her. He knew that keeping her safe would be long enough to discover her secrets. It wasn't long after her arrival that Ciri began pushing to start training, but Geralt warned her that it was too dangerous and that, despite her hatred for the Black Knight, they don't kill out of fear, but rather to save lives.


When they heard screams from the laboratory, Geralt left Ciri behind to investigate. He headed to the Great Hall and saw that Eskel had invited prostitutes to keep everyone entertained. One of them recognized Geralt, who had heard that he now had a daughter. Geralt told her that Ciri wasn't his daughter, and when the prostitute offered to take her in, he looked at her with disgust. Geralt confronted Vesemir, as witchers had to keep their stronghold a secret. But Vesemir assured him that by tomorrow, with stramonium, they would not remember anything. Geralt didn't like this and decided to confront Eskel, while Ciri was spying. Vesemir seemed happy that the witchers were happy; however, Geralt wanted to set an example. He told Eskel not to have fun inside Kaer Morhen. Eskel wasn't really in the mood for scolding. Think life was unfair. Geralt returned with a princess while the rest of them almost died on their missions. Eskel tried to hit Geralt, but he anticipated the blow and managed to subdue Eskel. He told Eskel to go to sleep. 


Geralt later asked Vesemir if he had seen Ciri. Vesemir jokingly told him that she was hitting a guy named "white seagull" while dancing on the table. Geralt laughed sarcastically and asked him the truth. He told Geralt that he had seen Ciri spying. He sent her to bed after talking to her. Vesemir wondered whether Geralt was ready to assume the duties of caring for and protecting Ciri. Geralt explained that he was in a cell in Cintra when it was sacked. He had heard everything: fires, screams, and deaths, the same sounds he used to hear as a child, the day Kaer Morhen fell. Vesemir was the only surviving witcher. He wondered if that day he was ready back then when he took him and others, and helped them become witchers. Vesemir admited that he didn't protect them because he wasn't prepared that once; he just taught them to fend for themselves. Geralt accepts that this is the best he can do for Ciri. Their conversation is interrupted when they feel all their medallions began vibrate, alerting the witchers to a danger in their home. Lambert got the prostitutes to safety, while Vesemir told Geralt to stay and fight instead of looking for Ciri. 

Geralt and the other witchers scattered to find the intruder. Entering the laboratory, Geralt discovered a leshy. Noted that the prostitute who was with Eskel before is dead. But when he noticed the witcher's medallion on his chest, to his surprise and confusion, Geralt looked at his face and saw that he was actually Eskel. However, when Vesemir's life was nearly taken, Geralt had no choice but to set his sword on fire and stabbed Eskel in the heart, killing him. 

This close call within the walls convinced Geralt it was time to teach Ciri how to defend herself.[10]

### Laying Eskel to Rest[]

This close call within the walls convinced Geralt it was time to teach Ciri how to defend herself.[10]

### Laying Eskel to Rest[]

There was anguish among the witchers when Geralt told Ciri to take a break from training. Lambert did not agree with Geralt killing Eskel. They had lost a brother. Geralt replied that what he had killed was not his brother. When Geralt left the Great Hall, he had a moment of reflection, remembering his past with Eskel. He went to the laboratory where Vesemir was searching for the cause of Eskel's transformation. He didn't want to give up, but Geralt told him it was time to let him rest. 

Geralt and Vesemir carried Eskel's body to a cave, where they laid his body to rest. Geralt felt as if the Continent was evolving underneath their feet. Still, Vesemir was determined to figure out what had happened and what he could have possibly missed in his tests. As the wolves arrived to consume Eskel's flesh, Geralt and Vesemir made their way out of the cave.

As Geralt patched her up, he told Ciri that just because she could do anything didn't mean that she had to, as Ciri wasn't afforded the same healing ability as witchers. Continued training with Coen, Geralt interrupted her training and asked Ciri to describe a strange sensation when something was chasing her. Geralt said that in the her parents' wedding feast, saw her mother, Pavetta, manifested an uncontrolled magical power, destroying the entire throne room. Apparently, Ciri has inherited that power. 

Geralt and Ciri followed the pull in her body, which led them to the very same leshy in the woods that had infected Eskel. ### Investigating a Monolith[]


Geralt continued training with Ciri, with the duo scaling mountains, walking across rocks, and running through the woods, where he reunited with Triss, who he invited to Kaer Morhen to help train Ciri, who likely inherited an evolved version of her mother's untrained magic. However, Ciri hadn't exhibited any typical indicators of Chaos. She only seemed to have the power of foresight, as well as a pull that led them to the leshy, leading Geralt to suspect that a mage could've sent the creatures to come after Ciri. Theoretically, Triss says it's possible, although skeptical about the creation of monsters. So she decided to perform a test to determine any signs of mutagen alchemy, but they wouldn't have results until morning. The two head off to bed. Haunted by the Battle of Sodden, Triss lists the names of her fallen friends, but Geralt's belief that believe that Yennefer is dead is almost unbearable, and he did not want to hear it. Triss then delivered a monologue about how the witchers pretend not to have feelings, but they know they do. She then shoots her shot with Geralt and suggests staying with her tonight, but he turned her down. 


In the morning, Geralt watched as Triss severely reprimands Lambert and Coen for ridiculing Ciri for dressing pretty and how they were treating her. In the laboratory, Geralt told Ciri that witchers felt bad for not finishing her breakfast. The Triss test results confirmed that there was no evidence of mutagenic alchemy. However, they uncovered stellacite, like from a monolith, both inside the leshy that turned Eskel and the creature Geralt killed, meaning they came from the same place, more specifically, the same monolith. It was then that Ciri revealed that when Nilfgaard attacked Cintra, just outside the city walls, she saw a monolith topple. Before she could reveal anything more, she touched the stellacite and had a vision about death to come. When she awakened in his bed, Geralt and Triss asked he to know everything she did. And so, Ciri revealed that when the Black Knight captured her, she screamed loudly and that was when the monolith cracked and fell. It was she who brought it down. Understanding this, Geralt decided to investigate for himself this connection and try to understand its meaning. 

Geralt prepares for his trip to Cintra when Triss appears with his elixirs. Regarding the night before, Geralt explained that he couldn't give her what she wanted or deserved, but for Triss, he was all she was looking for. His pain excited her because she finally felt something again. Most of them were cured after the battle, but some wounds could not be healed, like her burns. Geralt hoped that in her search to feel again, she'd find her value to him, as she was important to him. Vesemir appears and asks how someone who swore he would never return to Cintra twice now finds himself heading there for the third time, to which Geralt replied that he needs to do what he has to do to protect Ciri. Triss then opened a portal for Geralt, sending him to a mage named Istredd, an expert on monoliths who might be able to help him.[12]

Inside Cintra, while meeting with Istredd, Geralt informed him of his discovery and suspected that a new subspecies of monsters was emerging from a stellacite tower just outside Cintra, and that monsters had been nesting in the subterranean structure for years. With this theory in mind, they decided to investigate and crawl into the subterranean, where there was no nest or any evidence of life. Historians have always theorized that monoliths were scars from the Conjunction of the Spheres, but monsters didn't exist on their plane before the Conjunction. All species were on different planes until the spheres merged into a single one. A Conjunction like that would've required two things: a massive surge of energy and conduits to channel it, leading Istredd to suspect that the monoliths were actually conduits, meaning their monoliths were calling to the original spheres, opening a gateway between the spheres and the Continent.

Istredd wanted to know how Geralt knew the monsters and monoliths were linked. Still, Geralt was reluctant to tell him anything, as he didn't trust Istredd, who, in a moment of transparency, revealed that he actually came to Cintra because he thought a woman would be here, Yennefer. It's from Istredd that Geralt learned that Yennefer was truly alive. He sensed and realized that Istredd knew and loved her. Geralt's eyes lit up with hope upon hearing from him that Yennefer had survived after the Battle of Sodden. Suddenly, Geralt heard Ciri's scream and her cry for help. However, they were forced to take cover as shards of stellacite began flying at them. This resulted in a portal opening and a chernobog of some kind emerging and flying away.

Geralt traveled through a portal made by Istredd back to Kaer Morhen, where he intervened and stopped Vesemir, who, just before he could inject Ciri with a new witcher mutagen, created from her blood. Geralt unties her from her bonds and express his anger, telling Ciri that she didn't think about the consequences and could have died during the process. Ciri wanted to become a witcher so she would no longer have to feel the pain of her past. However, Geralt explained that no one could forget who they were, including witchers. Their best chance was to kill the hatred they held on to and move on.[13]

### Reuniting with Yennefer[]

### Reuniting with Yennefer[]

Geralt and Ciri hunted down the chernobog that escaped from the monolith. ### Hunting Down Yennefer[]

### Hunting Down Yennefer[]

On the other side of the stream, Geralt and Jaskier reunite with Yarpen and his crew, whom Geralt asked to borrow a horse from and would repay later.
