### Saving Ciri[]

### Saving Ciri[]

Geralt, angry at Yennefer but needing to get to Ciri, returned to Kaer Morhen, with an upset Yennefer following him. Yennefer tried to plead her case and apologize for her actions, noting that Voleth Meir knew how to find and exploit just the right weaknesses to make people do the demon's bidding, which, in Yennefer's case, meant even sacrificing a child. However, when she realized how special Ciri was to Geralt, she stopped at the last minute. This all fell on deaf ears, though, as Geralt was still angry at what she tried to do. 

When they arrived at the keep, they discovered that Ciri had been possessed by the Deathless Mother and found her in Vesemir's room, just as she was about to try to kill the sleeping witcher. The demon then tried to revert and pretend she was Ciri, but Geralt saw through her ruse, causing the demon to slice Geralt's face before running off.

With Vesemir awake now, Geralt tried to reason with the older witcher that killing Ciri wouldn't work, even if the Deathless Mother had already killed several witchers in their sleep. He then reminded him that Witchers killed to save lives, not out of fear, and that Ciri could be saved, but he'd need Vesemir's help to do so. 

They soon found Voleth Meir in the Great Hall, standing before the medallion tree, and Geralt offered himself up in exchange for Ciri, but Voleth Meir had no interest in this. The Deathless Mother, using Ciri's powers, then unleashed a mighty scream, cracking the medallion tree open and revealing a monolith hidden inside. She then shattered the monolith before opening a portal for two basilisks to exit, forcing the witchers to defend their home. Geralt asked Vesemir to trap him inside a barrier with Ciri so he could reach her.

During the commotion, Jaskier ran into the hall with active jasper, trying to get it to Geralt under Yennefer's instructions that it'd help free Ciri. However, as a third basilisk is summoned, it charges at Geralt and pushes him outside. Geralt, fortunately, managed to get the upper hand and slay the beast before rushing back in, only to see Vesemir, attempting to stop any more deaths, stab Ciri. However, she heals herself within seconds, proving his efforts futile.

Geralt, upon seeing the jasper and connecting it to Voleth Meir's remarks about them all feeling so much hatred and pain, realized what Yennefer had meant and got all the witchers to stop trying to kill, thereby removing the demon's ability to feed on their powers. However, the demon still refused to leave Ciri, making Geralt realize that her hut, which she had embodied, was burned and thus couldn't escape even if she wanted to, as she needed a vessel in their sphere. Yennefer then, seeing a way to right her wrongs, she decided to sacrifice herself for Ciri, offered herself up instead for the demon by slitting her wrists and, with Ciri having managed to awaken from the illusion she'd been under thanks to Geralt, pushed Voleth Meir out and to Yennefer.

While Voleth Meir slowly took possession, Geralt then asked Ciri to open a portal to the demon's native sphere to release her there, noting he believed in Ciri and that she could do this. With that, Ciri successfully created a portal, and she, Geralt, and Yennefer went through. Finally back home, Voleth Meir left Yennefer's body and instead linked up with the Wild Hunt that was galloping through the land to get to Ciri, who encouraged her as the "Daughter of Chaos" to join them. Still, Ciri managed to teleport herself, Geralt, and Yennefer back to Kaer Morhen.

Back home, Geralt discussed with Vesemir the realization that Ciri was being hunted, not just by various factions in their world, but the Wild Hunt as well. As such, they could no longer stay at Kaer Morhen, as they'd have to move constantly to avoid their enemies. Later, Yennefer also revealed she'd regained her powers, having felt it return when she sacrificed herself for Ciri. While Geralt hasn't forgiven her yet, and Yennefer longed for a fresh start, he knows she is the only person who helped Ciri control her powers. He also reminisced about when Borch Three Jackdaws noted that the two were destined to be together, but that destiny alone wasn't sufficient; something more was needed. Geralt then deduced that "something more" was Ciri.

Upon joined Ciri outside, Geralt and Yennefer assured her they'd see her along the way to her destiny, whatever it may be. Geralt revealed to Ciri about that he knew what Voleth Meir wanted from her. They had always known she came from another sphere. Ciri realized that her scream had awakened her, that was why she wanted her because she wanted to go home. He also understood that her powerful impulse screams each time Ciri shattered those monoliths attracted new species of monsters. But one thing that greatly concerned Geralt was that he couldn't figure out how Nilfgaard knew about Ciri before anyone else.[16]

### In search of a home[]

After leaving Kaer Morhen, in early 1265, the trio traveled constantly, staying at no one place for long to avoid those now trying to find and capture Ciri, as news had spread that the Princess of Cintra was alive. At one location, Geralt confronted and killed some men Rience had hired to find Ciri.

Yennefer began training Ciri while writing to Geralt constantly, reporting her progress. Starts each letter (for his irritatingly) with "Dear friend" while she slowly regain his trust. She was fully aware and accepting of the fact that Geralt hadn't yet fully forgiven her for her earlier transgressions, as he was still hurt and still had a hard time forgiving her for what had happened before, and hesitant to trust Yennefer again. Eventually, they're able to find a remote place to stay for a time thanks to Yarpen. Months pass, and the trio starts to feel like family. Over time, the trust between Geralt and Yennefer was restoring. Yarpen arrived with new information about various conflicts and realized that Geralt and Yennefer were fuckin again.


When Yarpen tells them that there will be a festival in Belleteyn, Ciri wants to go, despite Geralt and Yennefer's protests. Giving in, the trio attends that night to enjoy their first social gathering in six months, though incognito, as the event is known for its masks. Ciri is dressed and ready to go. Geralt, focusing on her safety, tells her to cover her eyes and her hair. Ciri gets mad because Geralt couldn't just say that she looked beautiful. Yennefer comes in, and Geralt, looking at her in a black dress—reminiscent of the one she wore when they first met, he then tells her she looks beautiful. At the festival, Ciri goes dancing, and Geralt and Yennefer begin to talk, recalling their beautiful nights they spent together over the decades, but in the momings one of them would be gone. Yennefer says she knows why she left, but Geralt isn't sure if he wanted to be in that kind of relationship or if it was just a trick of the djinn's magic. The three go into the maze, but the party is interrupted when Ciri is attacked by a jackapace, and Geralt and Yennefer manage to save her. 

Realizing their location has now been compromised, they set off on the road once more. Geralt, knowing it was Rience that sent the creature via some of Ciri's blood that was obtained at Kaer Morhen, the trio decides to prepare a trap for the mage so they can finish him off. 

With Yarpen's help, they spread rumors about a caravan secretly transporting a white-haired girl. To lend credibility to the rumors, Geralt turned to his faithful friend Jaskier to act as Ciri's partner. As expected, rumors reach Rience, who plans to attack the caravan.

They arrive at Shaerrawedd to take a break, where the statue of Aelirenn was located. Geralt and Yennefer shares with Ciri the tragic tale of Aelirenn, who was the first elf heroine to face the humans who led her young followers to death in this very place: "Neutrality. It won't get you a statue, but it will certainly help you stay alive." In the morning, Ciri shares a vision she had, reflecting on Aelirenn and what she and her followers fought for. Ciri wants to change the course, expressing a desire to change the cycle of violence, and bring balance and peace between both races. Geralt does not doubt her, but he does doubt the world. They suddenly detected that Rience was present, they got prepare to confront him. Rience arrives, accompanied by reinforcements to catch Ciri. This leads to a fight where Geralt is forced to abandon his neutrality to protect Ciri, battling against Rience's reinforcements in the ruins.

Yarpen leads his gang against Rience's men, while Geralt and Yennefer fight to protect Ciri. Rience escapes through a portal, and Geralt goes after him, while Yennefer keeps the portal open as long as possible. Geralt sees the place where they were through a window. As fighting the fire mage, he noticed arrows pierced the portal, so Geralt realizing something bed is happening at Shaerrawedd and that Yennefer won't be able to hold out much longer, so he breaks both of Rience's hands, neutralizing his magical abilities, and runs through the portal back to the ruins to help his friends.

He returned and saw that Shaerrawedd was suddenly ambushed by the elves led by Francesca, who also came for Ciri. Geralt quickly overwhelmed the elves, and they ordered a retreat due to many casualties. In the middle of the battle, Geralt acts to save Ciri from Francesca's brother, stabbed him in the process. Everyone gathers, and Geralt thanks Jaskier for his help and insists that he will survive; unfortunately, his lute was not so lucky. That night, Yennefer revealed that the portal used by Rience was born from a chaotic magic she had never felt before. This meant that a powerful dark mage was supporting Rience. They needed to advance Ciri's training further, and to do so, Yennefer proposes taking her to Aretuza, where she could receive training from Tissaia. Although this leads Geralt down a different path, he decides to track down Rience to finish him off, so they must separate, but they will meet soon.

He says goodbye to Ciri and Yennefer, the latter promising to look after Ciri. Because of this, Geralt reaffirms his trust and promises Yennefer that he will always think of her, no matter what happens. Later, Geralt reads another letter from Yennefer, in which she says that she and Ciri already miss him. He finally answers her and reveals that, for the first time, he understands what real fear is. Never see her and Ciri again.[17]

### Information from Rience's master[]

### Information from Rience's master[]

Geralt and Jaskier visit detectives Codringher and Fenn to find out about the mysterious mage of Rience. Unfortunately, Fenn claims they don't have enough coins to provide that information. Geralt then proposes Codringher a bet to throw a throwing star at him. If Codringher hits, it's game over; if it misses, they must give him the information. Codringher misses on purpose, as Geralt later reveals he heard him aiming to miss because he knew he wouldn't hit him. So, Fenn reveals that a sorcerer has his students running dirty deals across the continent. They do not know the mage's name, but they do know that he resides in Vuilpanne, an old castle located on the outskirts of Piana, built upon abandoned ancient scarlet ammonite mines of Redania. That would be the same castle that Geralt was already in when he was fighting Rience.

Having all the information they need, Geralt and Jaskier prepare to leave. However, Fenn's comment about them knowing who Ciri is stops Geralt, as he realizes that Istredd is one of their clients. They suggest getting a double who could pass of for Ciri and give her up so Ciri could be safe. Geralt didn't like hearing that. However, Geralt doesn't like the idea and refuses to sacrifice an innocent person to save Ciri. Jaskier tries to persuade Geralt to consider a more permanent solution to protect Ciri. Geralt decides to travel to Vuilpanne alone, not wanting to take Jaskier into further danger.

He arrives in Vuilpanne, and inside, Geralt begins to hear strange noises, so he drinks his witcher's elixir. He explores the castle dungeons and discovers a horrible experiment that appears to have gone wrong. He sees three heads of young girls emerging from a wall, attached to what look like bloody tentacles. They beg Geralt to help them. He listens, finds, and saves a girl with ashen-gray hair, who appears to have been unaffected by the grotesque experiments. When Geralt feels his medallion vibrate, he realizes the other girls are participating in the disturbing experience, and he sees a headless creature, fused from several bodies, arms, and legs, emerge. He was forced to kill the monster to save the young girl. 

Geralt carried the unconscious girl to a stream. Once she woke up, she said she knew he would como to save her. Confused, Geralt asked her who she was, and it turned out to his reaction of discovery that the girl he saved thinks she calls herself Ciri.[18]

### The Fake Ciri[]

In an attempt to find out what the young girl has, Geralt once again turned to Jaskier for help. They take her to Anika, who is a druid and an old friend of his mother's who might be able to help her. Anika lives with Otto Dussart, a werewolf, and another old friend that Geralt has known for years. He was hired to kill him, but instead he found a cure that prevented Otto's transforming. Geralt then asked how he and Anika had met, and Anika said that they met a year ago when they were both mourning at the Temple of Truth. Otto mourned his wife and children, who died in a fire, and Anika mourned Visenna. The news of his mother's death was a profound shock for Geralt. Anika shares that Visenna spoke often of him in her final days.

Anika discovers and deduced that the girl is under an extremely powerful mind-control spell that combines elements of chaos, druid magic, and elven sorcery. It also turns out that the girl is of elven blood. Geralt suspects that someone wants them to believe that she is Ciri. Anika gives her an elixir to help snap her out of the trance and verify the cause, but it will take time.

Waiting outside, Jaskier and Geralt start talking about the deal Jaskier made with Philippa Eilhart and Sigismund Dijkstra to bring Ciri to Redania. Geralt is aware of their reputation. Jaskier confesses him that he made a deal with they to bring Ciri to Redania, believing it to be the safest option for her protection from the Northern Kingdoms and Nilfgaard. Geralt rejects the proposal, knowing that Philippa and Dijkstra do not care about Ciri's safety, but rather want to use her as a political pawn to claim the throne of Cintra. While discussing her powers, Geralt hears Jaskier mention that Ciri is a "source". This triggers a memory of a conversation with the fake Ciri, who had previously mentioned the same ter. So he ran back to the house and woke her up. Anika urges Geralt to be careful, because it could alter the elixir's effectiveness.

The young girl revealed that her real name is "Teryn." She remembers the circumstances of her kidnapping, when she was abducted from her room by a man and a woman with a "strange voice." She said that the man who employed Rience was a mage from Aretuza. But suddenly, the effect of the elixir was altered, before the young girl could reveal more about the mage. Someone takes control of Teryn and tells Geralt that this man will come for Ciri. Teryn sends a magical blast in the direction of Geralt, Jaskier, Otto, and Anika. He also steals Otto's protective necklace, causing him to transform into a werewolf. Geralt keeps Otto subdued, while Jaskier tries to retrieve the amulet from Teryn. He throws it to Geralt, who quickly places it back on Otto, and Jaskier manages to calm the young girl with more elixir.


Later, Geralt sat next to Anika, who was recovering after being knocked out by Teryn, and told her how Visenna died. She was severely beaten after being mistaken for an elf while helping a villager. Geralt was left distraught by the news, forcing him to confront his past and the fact that his mother left him with the witchers when he was just a child. He remembers parts of his life, when they had to starve, and Visenna used her magic to create dishes they couldn't afford. He never forgave her for abandoning him, yet he never wanted her to suffer. Anika suggests that love for a child forces parents to make the most difficult decisions of their lives, and implying Visenna believed giving him up was the only way to save him. Distraught by the news and his past, Geralt confronts his trauma. He resolves that because he knows the pain of being abandoned, he will never abandon Ciri. Geralt leaves Teryn in the care of Anika and Otto, and sets out for Aretuza to reunite with Yennefer and Ciri 

Along the way, he found Ciri, who had recently separated from Yennefer in Gors Velen, having Geralt just arrived, saving her from ghostly horsemen, who turned out to be the Wild Hunt who were chasing Ciri. He shot magical blasts at them to make them disperse. Geralt and Ciri hugged each other after that terrifying moment. It was then that they noticed a piece of armor on the ground, which made Ciri realize that they were real.[19]

### Killing an Aeschna[]

### Killing an Aeschna[]

Upon learning that the Wild Hunt has escaped their sphere, Geralt explains to Ciri that it was because she left the "door open" when she left, meaning they have to go to Aretuza. Although she's not interested, it's the only place where she could be safe. Geralt asks her why she doesn't want to go, and Ciri basically replies it is because she doesn't like the conceited women there, but admits to feeling bad about harsh things she said to Yennefer, though Geralt assures her of forgiveness. He believes Ciri doesn't want to go because she is afraid of her powers. She believes Aretuza is the wrong move. Geralt tries to encourage her by telling her that if she accepts her powers, she will be able to access them whenever she wants, and that the only way to overcome this fear is to learn about them and use them.

They meet with Jaskier to board a ferry bound for Aretuza to get there faster than going riding. Seeing that they will not set sail due to the threat of a monster, Ciri convinces Geralt to offer her services in exchange for a free trip, if they kill the monster. Feeling safe in the presence of a witcher, the boatman, Obin, gladly accepts him. Jaskier is displeased when a musical group led by a rival of his, Valdo Marx, comes on board, having been invited to play at the conclave.

On board, Geralt talks to Ciri about her struggles with her magical abilities. Ciri thought that learning magic would make her a better leader. Now she thinks that maybe her grandmother was right: maybe it's better to rule with only steel. If necessary, Geralt begins a monologue about how nations are invisible lines that mean nothing but life that has real meaning, if she wants to be queen, then be queen, she would do an excellent job. When Valdo Marx and his company start singing in the middle of the trip, their song attracts the monster, an aeschna. The aeschna attacks one of Valdo's fellow musicians before Geralt and Ciri confront the creature. Their combat is fierce, and Ciri shows how much she has learned under Geralt's tutelage. Ciri delivers the final blow to the aeschna's head, an act that makes Geralt visibly proud.

After killing the aeschna, the trio reach the end of the journey and head to Aretuza. Ciri taunts him with the idea of ​​leaving the Continent's strife behind and forging a new life, hunting monsters for riches. In response, Geralt tells Ciri about the horrors he saw in Vuilpanne, where he saved Teryn, who, along with other young women, were part of a horrific experiment by the mage who supports Rience. Teryn, the only girl he saved, was brainwashed with Ciri's memories. Whoever is behind this wants to control Ciri's power. As such, they must go to Aretuza, reveal the truth, and take down Rience's master. Otherwise, they would only be condemning more innocent lives. Although Ciri is still unsure of her purpose, she knows that they must do whatever it takes to take down the mage responsible.

Once night falls, they reunite with Yennefer, who was waiting for them. She and Ciri apologize for what happened earlier, and both reconcile. Then, Yennefer entrusts Jaskier with Ciri's care for the night. Afterward, Geralt and Yennefer have a private conversation, which Jaskier and Ciri eavesdrop on, mimicking what they are saying. Geralt finally forgives Yennefer for her past mistakes, and they forgive each nother and reconcile, rekindling their love.

Later, Yennefer explained to him that someone had tried to kill her with a corrupted portal and that Geralt had appeared in the illusion. Discussing the clues they discovered, Geralt and Yennefer conclude that the mage behind everything is Stregobor, which makes sense considering his penchant for strange experiments with young women. Geralt wants to kill him, but Yennefer knows that they must first unmask him to the entire Brotherhood to prevent further chaos on the continent. Before the Mage Conclave took place, the Brotherhood organized a party on Thanedd Island so that people could mingle and release tensions. Geralt attends with Yennefer, dressed in a luxurious silver-and-black patterned suit, although he prefers his armor.[20]

### Aretuza ball[]


Entering the party, Yennefer introduces him to the well-known mages, though, surprised by Geralt's presence, the mages constantly monitor the witcher. She also asks him to behave himself. During the party, she introduces him to Sabrina Glevissig, who makes clear advances of telepathy towards him right in front of Yennefer. Still, Sabrina's flirtatious behavior does not fool Geralt. He later socializes with Philippa, who tells Geralt everything that happens at the ball, and Geralt wonders if she believes Rience's master is also present. Instead, Philippa informed him that the wine is laced with an aphrodisiac and that the caviar was an illusion. She even puts sex on the table, but Geralt rejects her without saying a word. They're interrupted by Dijkstra, who wishes to talk to the witcher alone. Once the men are alone, Dijkstra tries to convince Geralt to join his side and hand Ciri over to Redania, claiming she'll be safe with them. However, Geralt sees through this ploy and rejects the offer. 

Geralt saw how the Stregobor board of directors was being rude to the staff and intervened. Geralt threatens him, demanding he pay for everything he did. Stregobor saw that he had not over Renfri's death and claimed that it was he who stabbed her with the dagger after all. Also, he is determined to save the continent from monsters like Geralt, but the witcher says he doesn't do anything like Stregobor.


After walking through the hallways above, Geralt enters the Gallery of Glory, where he meets Vilgefortz of Roggeveen, who shows him the paint that is known as "The First Arrival" when the Brotherhood was forged on the coast, which's also his favorite paint. Vilgefortz then insists that the two have more in common. He reveals that he was an orphan who had a difficult life. He didn't fit the labels of mage, human, or druid, so he decided to become a sorcerer. Vilgefortz says he changed after meeting Tissaia. Seeing Yennefer talking to Istredd, Vilgefortz tells Geralt that they were once lovers. First loves are difficult to forget. Vilgefortz tried to convince him to get on the right side and align with his faction within the Brotherhood. Geralt refuses to be drawn into the political machinations of the sorcerers, insisting that he adapts to the world around him rather than choosing sides. Vilgefortz argues that by failing to pick a side, Geralt will be surrounded by enemies perpetually. 


A short time later, he finds Yennefer talking with Istredd, and Yennefer tells Geralt that Istredd was telling her about a dangerous Book of Monoliths that Stregobor has, which makes them suspect he might be behind everything happening on the continent, but they need evidence. Before more can be said, the formal dancing starts, in which Geralt must participate. As Geralt rotates partners, he finds himself dancing with Lydia van Bredevoort, whom he notices when he asks if she's enjoying the dance; she doesn't say a word. Another sorceress, Marti Södergren, threw herself at Geralt, telling him that she had been wanting to get to him all night. In her obvious attempts to seduce the witcher, she told him about her extraordinary flexibility, although Geralt tried to ignore her before continuing with the partners rotation. He then dances with Triss, who wonders about Ciri's safety, though Geralt reassures her that Ciri is safe for now. Exchanging partners and back to dancing with Yennefer, he tells her that he will create a distraction so she can sneak into Stregobor's office. Geralt then brushes up to Istredd and tells him to play along, and the two pretend to fight over Yennefer, distracting everyone and allowing Yennefer to sneak off. 

However, unbeknownst to the trio, Stregebor had a security measure in place that alerted him to someone snooping in his office, so he left the ballroom. Geralt followed behind, allowing him and Yennefer to confront Stregobor about the kidnapped noivces and torturing them to get to Ciri. In the midst of this, Tissaia, Vilgefortz, Istredd, Triss, and Artorius Vigo arrive while Geralt and Yennefer bring up the fact that he has a list of all the missing elvish novices and has been practicing mind control on them. Stregobor protests this, having no idea what they're talking about, as Istredd finds the book of monoliths in the safe. Stregobor looks somewhat puzzled by the book being among his possessions, but the evidence says it all, and Tissaia proposes to lock him up until the Conclave and be judged.

At the end of the evening, everyone toasts the alliance between all the mages of the north. In the process, they give special thanks to Yennefer, who designed this event. On this occasion, Geralt confessed his love to Yennefer for the first time, surprising her by saying it is the first time he has ever told her. The two then kissed in front of everyone.


Later that same night, Yennefer tells Geralt about her conversation with Philippa and how Philippa tried to persuade her to join her rather than serve the Brotherhood. Philippa also noted that Tissaia is a lot like Lydia, blinded by love, and that she would follow her lover wherever she went. As they unwind in their private room, feeling accomplished at having managed to thwart plans to get Ciri, something troubles Geralt until he realizes they were wrong. Connecting the dots, he realizes Lydia was the mage who couldn't speak and was communicating telepathically as the woman of the "strange voice" that Teryn mentioned, and that Tissaia's bracelet, which the sorceress had lost during Stregobor's arrest, and Yennefer had recovered earlier, matched the same red stone that was in the pair of earrings Lydia wore at the dance. They realize the scarlet ammonite itself can only be found in the mines of West Redania, the same location where Geralt found Teryn and the missing girls. As the only survivor, Teryn revealed that Rience worked together with a familiar face from Aretuza. By connecting Vilgefortz's earlier conversation with him regarding joining the war, his favorite painting, and the location of the mines, Geralt and Yennefer deduced that the mage responsible for all the events was actually Vilgefortz, not Stregobor, was the mastermind behind Rience and the hunt for Ciri. 

Yennefer stays in the room and uses a locator spell to find Tissaia, while Geralt clears the halls to clear their path. However, once Geralt leaves the room, he hears the sounds of battle already beginning to echo through the hallways. Just right, Dijkstra comes out of the shadows, surprising him with a dagger to Geralt's neck, and says that Geralt should have chosen a side.[21]

### Thanedd coup[]

### Thanedd coup[]

After hearing the screams in the hallways, and being cornered by Dijkstra, the master spy reveals to Geralt that he and Phillipa have planned a coup d'état, taking Aretuza as a hostage, since the largest kingdom in the North has tired of the mages who plot on their behalf, rather than working to unite the continent against the invaders of Nilfgaard. The Redanians aim to rid the Brotherhood of Sorcerers who have allied themselves with Nilfgaard. They have used dimeritium to suppress the magical powers of Aretuza's traitor mages. In turn, Philippa launched an anti-magic dome around Aretuza to ensure the success of the invasion of Redania. Since Geralt has no particular problem with Redania, he decided to leave his sword behind and see how things develop. Furthermore, he already knows that Vilgefortz is behind all the events on the continent, which means he benefits from letting Dijkstra expose the traitor.

However, the plan goes wrong when they try to expose Vilgefortz, claiming that he is an ally of Nilfgaard. Tissaia arrives and believe Dijkstra and Philippa are the traitors, and Geralt, who sits in the corner uninvolved, sees a mist in the bay, claiming that someone is using magic to hide ships. They imagine it to be the army of Redania, about to land on the coast of Thanedd to reinforce their betrayal. Blinded by her love for Vilgefortz, Tissaia dismantles Phillipa's dome and frees her fellow mages. During the following conflict, Geralt confronted and fought Dijkstra, breaking his leg for trying to kidnap Ciri.

Once outside Aretuza, Geralt found and saved Ciri and Yennefer from Rience, who attempted to catch Ciri again, just as Yennefer threw his sword, appeared behind him and dealt the final blow, decapitating Rience, finally ending his life. Geralt explained to Ciri that both Redania and Nilfagaard are here for her, and Vilgefortz was the mage responsible, and had brought both Nilfagaard and the Scoia'tael. They decide to flee the island through the ferry chain. But then, Yennefer senses Tissaia summoning the powerful, last-resort spell Alzur's Thunder and feels she must return to support her, sensing the severity of the situation, despite Geralt's objection to separating. Yennefer doesn't want to abandon Ciri, but Ciri understood what Yennefer meant to her and that she had to help Tissaia. Yennefer makes the difficult decision to leave Ciri and Geralt to support her mentor, but promised to return with them soon. Before departing, Yennefer hugs Ciri and calls her "her daughter."

In the middle of the Thanedd coup, Geralt and Ciri are found by Cahir, the Black Knight, whom Ciri still hates and wants to kill him for destroying her home and haunted her in dreams. As revenge, Geralt reminds her that when her does it, there will be no turning back. Surprisingly, Cahir does not want to fight. He admitted to following brutal orders without thinking, specifically during the fall of Cintra, but has now realized his mistakes, and he offers his life in exchange for Ciri's forgiveness. As Scoia'tael warriors approach to capture her, Cahir stays behind to face them, effectively providing a distraction to allow Geralt and Ciri to escape.

They tried to escape in a boat, and Geralt sensed danger through his medallion. He asked Ciri to run, giving her his final promise that they would always find each other, and she ran away towards Tor Lara. Upon coming face to face with Vilgefortz, Geralt drew his sword. The mage offered him one last time to join him, but the witcher rejected him again. The two engage in a huge fight on the beach. Geralt believes he can finish him off, but the mage reveals the power that he has been holding back to pretend that he was weaker than he really was. Vilgefortz inflicts a series of serious wounds on Geralt, including breaking his back and leg, and shattering his steel sword. Leaving him alive to suffer, the mage then went after Ciri, but she managed to escape through the Benavent's portal in the tower, which then exploded. Geralt is found and saved by Triss with her last strength and taken to the Brokilon Forest to be healed by the dryads.[22]

The dryads begin to treat the witcher, who endures his wounds with extraordinary resistance and does not even lose consciousness. Geralt speaks to them in their language, urging them not to waste time, but Queen Eithné says it's not a waste, and shows him his brooch. Triss had asked her to tell him that something awaits him out there. Eithné also confirmed him that Ciri was once their guest. 

Jaskier arrived in Brokilon and finds him resting, where he informs him that Yennefer was fine, but that Ciri had disappeared. Also, that Emperor Emhyr has devastated many northern villages in search of her and has offered a large reward for information about Ciri. In a letter Jaskier had, Geralt learned that she had apparently been found and was on her way to Nilfgaard.[23]

### Treated by the Dryads[]

### Treated by the Dryads[]

Geralt is desperate to go save Ciri but had to stay in Brokilon because of his very bad condition. His thigh and leg were shattered. He is cared for by Milva, a skilled human archer, charged by Queen Eithné to care for him while he recovers. Jaskier sits next to him, as the dryads attempt to use the healing water to treat his wounds. Unfortunately, it didn't work the healings waters had no effect on him due his mutation. As for Geralt, he's ready to go right now despite he cannot fight, but Milva tried to convince him that he was in no condition that he is not fit to go to find his daughter and face certain death.

Geralt tried to train, but Milva showed him that he is not yet capable of going to save Ciri. Later, she comforted him and asked about the brooch, Geralt explained that it reminds him of someone he killed. His encounter with Renfri in Blaviken was a deeply traumatic experience for him, leaving him with a heavy burden and a feeling of guilt, and the realization that life always forces one to make a choice. He always kept the brooch because always served as a reminder of the lesson she gave him to remind him to stay out of affairs that don't involve him—that getting involved in human affairs, or trying to manage fate, leads to catastrophe.

That night, while resting, Geralt received a visit from Yennefer, whom he was very relieved to see. She informed him that Ciri was not with her, but Geralt pointed out that it was his fault, he had let Vilgefortz defeat him, he couldn't protect her. Yennefer also informs of the tragic suicide of Tissaia. They both blame each other for the loss of Ciri, while Geralt begins to shed tears. Although the dryads had done all they could, but they could not fully heal him, Geralt asks Yennefer to use her magic. While she notes that magic cannot heal some wounds, Geralt promises her to find Ciri and make both Vilgefortz and Emhyr pay for what they have done. Yennefer then use her magic to speed Geralt's healing.

Upon recovering the next day, Geralt encounters a young elf named Dara, who told him that he once had met Ciri a long time ago, and asks him to pass a message to Ciri: that he forgives her and was truly sorry for how things ended between them. Geralt and Jaskier prepare an improvised version of the elixir. Geralt drinks it and resumes his training with the dryads to sharpen his senses while he prepares.

Geralt and Jaskier are at a checkpoint while trying to reach Nilfgaard. Although they do not have the papers, Geralt bribes a border guard and offered the brooch as payment, which the guard accepted. As they continued on their way, they stopped when they notice the guard abusing and rejecting a family by taking a little girl her doll. Despite Jaskier's pleas to avoid trouble, Geralt, who alwayed adhered to his rule of never intervening in other people's conflicts, breaks his long-standing policy of neutrality and decides to act against the cruelty. He go into action and kill all the soldiers at the checkpoint. Milva arrived in time and quickly killed three handfuls of soldiers. She decided to join their company. Geralt leaves the guard alive, instructing him to tell his Emperor that Geralt will come and free Ciri. After returning the doll to the little girl, the three took some horses and continued on their way.[24]

### A mission to Nilfgaard[]


Around 1266, Geralt was on the path with Milva and Jaskier, traveling across the war-torn countryside toward Nilfgaard. They see a burning village in the distance, which has fallen to the Nilfgaardians. They head into a woods, where they find a caravan with corpses. Geralt claimed they're Havekars, essentially corpse robbers who sell their scavenged items to the highest bidders. He was ambushed as he explored the scene and killed the assailants. Geralt then found out what the caravan was transporting, the Nilfgaardian knight Cahir, locked in a coffin, bound, gagged, and locked inside. Geralt apparently is disliked the guy and wanted to kill him for tormenting Ciri, but Jaskier and Milva ask him for mercy. Geralt decides to spare Cahir's life, attributing this merciful streak to the fact that Ciri did as well on Thanedd. But he tells him that if he ever crosses their path again, he will kill him. Geralt then leaves his knife for Cahir to escape on his own, as the shouts of approaching reinforcements fill the woods and Geralt, Jaskier, and Milva abandon the scene. 

Later, Geralt was still treat his leg wound, which hadn't fully healed since his brutal battle with Vilgefortz. But no matter how much he used the brokilon water, it not helping. Milva tried to talk about Cahir, explaining that despite being the man who kidnapped Ciri, he was a prisoner of the men who attacked him, but Geralt clearly still considered him an enemy. Geralt plans to ride south to the Yaruga River, avoiding as much of the growing war between Nilfgaard and the Northern Kingdoms as possible on the way. For the way, the group encountered a dwarf and a gnome called Zoltan Chivay and Percival Schuttenbach, refugees they're escorting north, and a foul-mouthed parrot named Field Marshal Windbag. The dwarf recognized Geralt as the White Wolf, and Jaskier introduced himself by his real full name and title, and finally, Milva of the Woods.

Geralt noted that it's bold to sing while walking down the highway, and Zoltan commented that it's better than weeping, given the bodies littered along the roads. Zoltan then asked where they were going, and Jaskier nearly said "Nilfgaard," but Geralt interjected, "nowhere." Hearing this, Zoltan demanded to know why they'd go to that place, and Jaskier tried to answer again, saying that Geralt wanted to save his daughter. However, Geralt again interjected, stating there is no reason. Understanding the internal strife within the group, Zoltan stated that his group is heading east and that they can go together until their paths part. Still, Geralt declined, stating their journey was too dangerous, but Zoltan argued that it was even better, as safety in numbers was a virtue. Jaskier interjected this time, trying to decline, but after Percival stated that his group had food, Jaskier immediately agreed to the offer.

That night, Geralt sits by a small campfire, trying to adjust his leg to a comfortable position. Milva asked if he was in pain. Geralt answers no, and Milva thinks he was bluffing, prompting Geralt to ask why she'd asked if she already knew. Milva says it's because that's how conversations work, and in Brokilon he never said what monster caused it, but Jaskier argues that he wouldn't say it like that. She asked what kind, and Geralt stated the worst kind, the human kind.

Percival and Zoltan join the group by the fire with bread, cheese, and haggis. Geralt then asked how they felt about robbing people, but Zoltan defended himself, saying he's a good person who takes care of those in his circle, including Geralt's group. Before leaving, Zoltan offered to have Percy and his group steal some good weapons like his own rune-inscribed sword. Geralt asked what was wrong with his own sword, which Zoltan said was busted, and Geralt got up, saying they'd leave in the morning. Geralt, still adjusting to the loss of Ciri and Yennefer, as well as the loss of his equipment in Thanedd, remains distant and focused on his journey.

By morning, Geralt awakened and prepared Roach for setting off, but Milva approached him and admonished him from going off alone as Jaskier awakened. They were concerned about him, and Geralt confessed that he had another dream featuring Ciri, who was happily dancing somewhere, but so was death. He also confessed that he believed this was Ciri's new destiny: fire in front of her and death behind her. He also worries that he cannot save her. Jaskier grabbed his belongings and suggested they go, as Zoltan calls out to them, asking if they're ready to head out.


The group passed across a farmstead, and Percy caught the scent of porridge and milk. They wanted to steal the cow and escape quickly, but when Percy went to investigate, a young girl came out of the house and warned them that she was infested with pox. Percy alerted the rest of the group, and they continued on their way. However, they see a group of soldiers pull up in front of the house. The young girl tried to warn them to stay back, that it was a pox-ridden area, but they didn't care and dragged her to the inside into the house. Seeing the young girl attempt to assault her sexually by the soldiers, Geralt took Zoltan's sword and decided to intervene. He killed most of them with his sword and then with a hook he had left, and Milva killed the last one with an arrow after Geralt injured his leg. A surviving one rides off, and Milva tries to kill him with an arrow, but misses. The group approaches and Geralt informs them that the place is not infested with pox, was a ruse created by the young girl to try to survive. 

Geralt offered to take her to a safe place, but the young girl retreated into her house, and Zoltan called her ungrateful for what they did for her, even though Milva angrily defended her. They then looked the same soldier who got away return, only that behind him was Cahir who had killed him, and who had followed the group. Although Geralt prepares to kill him, Milva steps in, and Cahir leaves. Stealing the boots from one of the dead men, Geralt gave them to Jaskier, who, although advised against it before, was more accepting of it now.[25]

### A night in the Fen Carn graveyard[]

### A night in the Fen Carn graveyard[]

Geralt knew of a shortcut through the Fen Carn graveyard to reach Nilfgaard, allowing them to avoid any battlefields by traversing the ruins. Upon arriving at the entrance, Geralt and his traveling companions encounter two guys attempting to collect a bounty on a supposed monster roaming the area, offered by their priest. The guys then insult Milva and try to steal her horse, earning one of them a punch in the face before those two left.

Geralt ordered Percival and the others to stay back while he, Jaskier, Milva, and Zoltan advanced to cross safely and secure the passage. Inside the cemetery, Jaskier was suddenly drawn into a specter after inadvertently reading an inscription on a tombstone, just as Geralt tried to warn him. Milva and Zoltan went into the tomb to help Jaskier while Geralt lured the specter into him. So, Geralt gets dragged around by the specter trying to take him down to the tomb. Every attack Geralt tries with his sword phases through it. He breaks free from the specter, slides on the ground, and sets a trap for the specter by using the sign Aard to trap it. The specter walks into it, and Geralt can grab its heart, and he crushes it in his hand, putting the specter's soul to rest. The others come out of the tomb relatively unscathed. Milva asked how it felt to kill that beast, but Geralt said it wasn't a beast; that was its heart, consumed by a lifetime of sorrow. Its suffering is over.

As they are walking back to reunite with Percival and their other traveling companions, since night had fallen, Geralt, Jaskier, Milva, and Zoltan hear a noise in the graveyard and come across with a intriguing barber-surgeon named Emiel Regis. He claimed to be a herbalist who lives in the area, hiding in the graveyard to avoid the war. Catching a glimpse of Geralt's injuries, Regis offers assistance and welcomes the group to stay the night at his cottage, offering them hospitality. Geralt thinks it's a good idea and tells them, "Let's gather the others."

They enter the little cottage, and Regis provides a unique mandrake-infused concoction to the group. While Jaskier, Milva, Zoltan, and Percy partaking of Regis' home-brewed liquor, he quietly invites Geralt into a side room to tend to his leg wound. Regis notes that Geralt used magic to heal himself instead of resting, which is the reason he is having issues. Geralt makes it clear he wants no one to know about his injury. Regis agrees and rewraps his leg with some herbs that can help with the pain.

While Jaskier, Milva, Zoltan, and Percy get drunk, and Geralt notices that Regis isn't drinking, who affirms that his health isn't what it once was. The potent brew makes Jaskier and the others highly talkative, leading Jaskier to reveal Regis the details of Geralt's mission to find Ciri. It turns out that Regis, as Geralt realizes, was getting them drunk to loosen their tongues, to which Regis replies that it was deliberate, in part to make them honest enough with themselves for him to see if he could trust them. He also mentions that many say mandrake makes them reveal their deepest wishes. Geralt doesn't believe in the wishes and, annoyed, walks out of the house. He goes out to outside and about a log in the forest falling asleep. Under the influence of the mandrake, made Geralt dream of a peaceful, conventional life with Yennefer and Ciri in a cottage, culminating in him and Yennefer dying of old age.

Upon waking from his dream in the morning, seeing all this, Geralt went back to the house, where Regis told him he was the last to wake and that the others were waiting for him on the road. Geralt confesses to Regis that 40 days have passed since he left Brokilon, but he has only traveled 50 of the 200 leagues remaining to reach Emhyr's palace. He needs to act faster if he wants to save Ciri. Sympathetic to Geralt's quest, Regis is apologetic for drugging them and even offers to join them so that he can look after Geralt's wound. He is vague about his reasons, citing that he doesn't want to be alone anymore. Regis even advises Geralt to focus on the joy of his journey with his companions, rather than the fear of his previous, harsher existence. As they prepare to leave, Geralt notices a flower crown worn by Beata, the refugee girl, which is identical to one he saw in his dream. As they head out, Regis takes the old, bloody bandage from Geralt's wound and inhales the blood.[26]

### Trial by Ordeal[]

Riding on Roach while Regis rides beside him, Regis informs Geralt that they're closing in on their destination, which Geralt questions, as he doesn't know how Regis knows that. Regis offers no answer, but their party then passes by a mound of corpses, which makes Jaskier want to go a different direction, but Geralt insists they continue forth. Beata told Geralt she believed her family would be at the refugee camp ahead, but Jaskier warned that the Nilfgaardian forces were close behind and asked whether they should continue. Geralt again states that they should, and they venture forth.

Upon arriving at the refugee camp, two of the refugees in their party reunited with their families, and Geralt and Jaskier also met up with Yarpen there. Seeing Beata run off into a large crowd, Geralt follows her to a crowd of people, and once he catches up to her, learns from Beata that her sister Talver was there. They soon discover that Talver was set to be burned at the stake for being a witch, and Beata rushes to her sister, who is then accused of practicing witchcraft as well. The same two villagers that Geralt and his party encountered at the cemetery before were the ones who accused Talver of witchcraft. Their instigation of Milva made Geralt want to solve the issue with his sword, but Regis admonished him from doing so, as it would do them no favors in their predicament.


The priest in charge of the witch trial proposes that if Geralt can prove the two girls are witches, then he and his companions are free to go, but Geralt wants to hear proof of the claims against the girls. One of the bandits accuses Talver of using his cat for ingredients to prepare one of her potions. However, Zoltan describes the cat in detail and points out that it was close by. Despite the revelation, the crowd believed Talver had resurrected it, and the priest tried to have she and her sister burned, but Geralt proposed an alternative: a trial by combat. Geralt challenged the priest to a duel, but the priest stated that they already have an alternative: a trial by ordeal. The trial was that someone had to pull a piping-hot horseshoe from a small cauldron without being burned. Stepping up to the task, Regis easily performs this task, and amid the uproar from the crowd, the Nilfgaardian army arrives, causing the crowd to scatter. Geralt then rescues Talver and Beata from being burned at the stake, which was now surrounded by an ignited fire. 

Running across a small field trying to reach their wagon, Geralt witnesses Beata's throat sliced open by a Nilfgaardian soldier, and with Beata dying in his arms, he tries to console her, but she dies. Holding the deceased Beata in his arms, Geralt tells Talver to flee, and after she does, a soldier knocks Geralt out.[27]

### Captured by Redanian Forces[]

### Captured by Redanian Forces[]

Awakening from Jaskier's calls to him, Geralt found himself tied up beside his friend in a Redanian base camp and is then debriefed by Jaskier about what had happened while he was knocked out. A high-ranking Cintrian soldier approaches them and immediately accuses them of being Nilfgaardian spies. However, Geralt deny the soldier's accusation, and adds they're not enemies of the late Queen Calanthe, and Geralt's last remark causes the soldier to snap at him, demanding he not say the name of his late queen. The soldier then details that he was at there the day when Geralt invoked the Law of Surprise, and he believed he caused the queen to die and for Cirilla to fall into the hands of Emhyr. Finished with his diatribe, the soldier calls over two more soldiers to take Jaskier and Geralt to be executed, despite Geralt clarifying that they are making a mistake.

Somewhere else in the camp, Dijkstra vents his frustrations onto a tree until a servant named Eva approaches him and informs him of the news of the detained Geralt and Jaskier. The news prompts Dijkstra to order Eva to prevent Geralt and Jaskier's execution by the Cintrian soldiers, and to have the bard meet with King Radovid. Though Geralt is taken to a tent where he's chained to a chair, he's soon joined by an elated Dijkstra and the revenge-filled Cintrian soldier. Much to the soldier's disapproval, Dijkstra orders him to leave Geralt and him; however, the soldier demands that he stay, but Dijkstra reminds him that Cintra is in Redania's debt. Hence, the soldier begrudgingly leaves the tent, allowing Dijkstra and Geralt to be alone. Walking over to Geralt, Dijkstra wacks Geralt's wounded leg with his cane, and details that because of it, he now has to walk using a cane. Geralt makes a sarcastic remark, prompting Dijkstra to clutch Geralt's leg and praise him for his tenacity.

Taking a nearby chair, Dijkstra sits on it and tells Geralt that his arrival has been fortuitous, though then remarks that he'll still die regardless. Geralt then rhetorically asks why everyone wants to make a sermon of his death and follows up by asking why Dijkstra serves a king who will soon be replaced. To that question, Dijkstra lifts himself off his chair and, while fetching a metal quill from another table, tells Geralt that everyone has a purpose, even the bard. With the quill in his hand, Dijkstra states that from then on, nothing is personal, and Geralt asks why he wants him dead, but Dijkstra calmly replies that not everything is about him.

Meanwhile, Jaskier speaks to Radovid, explaining that he and Geralt are still journeying to locate Ciri, but can't continue because they're accused of being Nilfgaardian spies. So, Radovid offers to pardon the two; however, back in the tent, Dijkstra uses the metal quill to stab him in the neck, making him wince in pain. Still, Geralt defiantly states that the pain Dijkstra is causing him is nothing compared to the pain he's currently experiencing. Regardless, Dijkstra continues his torture and taunts Geralt that he'll never see Ciri again and demands that he scream so loud that the entire camp would hear him. Succumbing to the pain, Geralt gives Dijkstra what he wants, and his screams reach the ears of Jaskier, who was still with Radovid, and it causes a falling out between them.

After finishing his torture of Geralt, Dijkstra thanked him for his service and told him that Emhyr plans to marry Ciri. Dijkstra also states that he'll return him to Vissegerd, the Cintrian soldier with a vendetta against him. Reaching a fever pitch of rage, Geralt breaks free of his confines and tries to attack Dijkstra, but is stopped by two Redanian soldiers, and taking advantage of the situation, Dijkstra gleefully taunts Geralt.

Afterward, Geralt is joined by Jaskier inside a new tent, and the two discuss the plan from there on out as they only have until morning to avoid their execution. Jaskier then informs Geralt of his meeting with Radovid, which was initially cordial but, when it came to choosing between Radovid and Geralt, obviously chose the latter. Hearing this, Geralt confesses that Dijkstra caused the rift between them by torturing him and adds that Beata was dead, which Jaskier already knew, and apologizes for her loss. Curiously, Geralt asks whether their companions and the people in the villages are dead, and Jaskier gives no answer. Geralt then admits that he saw Ciri in a dream where she's not followed by death, but is being followed by it, and he adds that she's to wed Emhyr, which Jaskier then states they need to consider themselves for the time being.

Eventually, Vissigerd arrives and wants to kill the two using a razor that belonged to Queen Calanthe, but is stopped by Regis, who then frees the two. Regis then informs the two that Milva and the others aren't too far behind, and although Geralt was grateful toward Regis, he asks that Regis part ways with them. Understanding Geralt's plea, he hands Geralt an elixir that would prove useful to him and allows the two to escape.

Outside, as Jaskier helps Geralt walk, Jaskier asks Geralt who Regis was, and Geralt answers a vampire, which shocks Jaskier. They reach the base's front gate, and after an incident involving Jaskier and the guards stationed there, the group rejoins them as Nilfgaardian soldiers ambush the base. Amid the chaos, Geralt takes the elixir that Regis gave him and, now in his mutant form, fights off against the Nilfgaardian soldiers, where he sees Cahir. Although the former Nilfgaardian soldier claims he's no longer his enemy, Geralt is reluctant to believe him and is forced to leave him after seeing Jaskier wounded. So, Geralt and the others are forced to leave the camp as fiery explosions engulf it.[28]

### A shocking truth comes to light[]

### A shocking truth comes to light[]

After escaping the attack on the Redanian camp, the group camps in a woods beside a river to rest while Jaskier recovers from his bandaged head wound during the flight. But Geralt doesn't want to waste any more time to save Ciri, haunted by the knowledge that now he knows she will marry Emhyr. He decides to cross the river immediately if they want to reach Nilfgaard as soon as possible, despite Milva's insistence. She insists they need to rest to allow Jaskier and their horses to recove. She then volunteers to scout the crossing.

Geralt rejoins the others and tries to help Jaskier to his feet. Cahir, who is now with them, advises him to let him rest. Geralt and Cahir then have a brief confrontation. Geralt still refuses to accept that Cahir joined them after what he did to Ciri, hunting her. But Cahir reveals that they have more in common. He, too, has been dreaming of Ciri, dreams that seem like omens, though Geralt refuses to listen. Drawing the knife he left behind, Cahir gives Geralt a choice: kill him now if he regrets sparing his life, as Ciri did, or he can listen to him and allow him to join them. Before the situation escalates, Milva returns to report that the crossing is flooded. So they must wait for it to clear or return to the camp they barely escaped. Jaskier also needs to rest, and everyone else needs to regain their strength.

While they wait to cross, the group prepares a stew for lunch, but Geralt wants to find another crossing. However, Milva and Jaskier convince him to stay until they both recover.


Everyone immediately notices the recent tension between Yarpen and Zoltan, who don't get along, and learns that Zoltan had been exiled from Mahakam for treason by the dwarf councilman Brouver Hoog. To pass the time, Jaskier suggests they recount what happened. Yarpen explains that in Mahakam, Zoltan ran a successful forge. He manufactured weapons, and Yarpen delivered them to Brouver, who shipped them down to the dwarven front lines. Zoltan was indeed exiled, ostensibly for treason by supplying weapons to humans. However, Zoltan reveals that this charge was a fabrication by Brouver. In reality, Brouver was the one delivering dwarven weapons to human factions who subsequently used them to kill other dwarves. Upon discovering Brouver's betrayal, Zoltan stopped forging weapons for him. In retaliation, Brouver orchestrated the burning of Zoltan's forge and, using his immense influence, ruined Zoltan's reputation and forced him into exile. Having previously believed Zoltan to be a traitor, Yarpen learns the truth and reconciles with him. 

While the group prepares soup, Milva offers some root vegetables she learned to cook with in Brokilon. Despite Geralt's attempts to revisit the river crossing, Jaskier encourages Milva to share how she ended up in Brokilon. She never talks about it and doesn't want to. But his sincerity and interest are such that she can't resist.

Milva recounts how her stepfather constantly abused her when she was young until her rage finally consumed her and she killed him, a deed she felt was worthwhile. She fled to the forest, fearing the consequences. She lived in the woods for a time, where did what was necessary to survive on her own. She finally encountered and saved a group of dryads from humans, the dryads offered her refuge in Brokilon Forest where she found a home among them. While in Brokilon, she began helped escort a group of Scoia'tael elves warriors through the woods to protect them from human forces. In her retelling, she shares how on a previous mission, she was celebrating with the group of Scoia'tael warriors she was escorting, and how she had engaged in a sexual liaison with one of the elves. But to the next day Milva was heartbroken, since they had been ambushed and all were slaughtered. This event made her step back from that role. She was later tasked when found a new task to help Geralt healing.


Shortly after, with Jaskier pressuring everyone, the group unites and demands that he tell them what he's been writing. He plans to write a book of poems, admitting that he's getting old and won't be around much longer, but that his stories might live on. Jaskier then begins to sing, prompting Zoltan to question whether every story has to be told through song, to which Jaskier, slightly offended by the question, replies that it does. He recounts his days in Oxenfurt with Geralt, who remarks that his memories of their time together are slightly different. His story revolves around the time Jaskier discovered his rival, Valdo Marx, whom he recalls as a ragged street performer. He saw potential in him and taught him the art of poetry. However, Valdo stole Jaskier's valuable songbook and began passing off his mentor's songs as his own, achieving enormous popularity. Because of this, Jaskier developed a lifelong resentment toward Valdo. But he concludes by saying that the stories in this book will outlast Valdo and any song he may have stolen, from what would one day be "50 Years of Poetry." The dwarves and the gnome give him a standing ovation. 

At that moment, Regis appears. Everyone moves away from him, now knowing he's a vampire. Geralt reminded him not to see they again, but Regis claims he's only there to tend to the poet's wound. The bard leaves him no choice but to heal him. Regis notices they hadn't realized they were out of spices for their soup. His suggestion: basil, pepper, sage, and bay leaf. Regis says he heard Jaskier's tale, so he advises that "Half a Century of Poetry" would be a slightly more poetic title than "50 Years." Jaskier doesn't mind.


Geralt was about to ask if it was over so he could leave, but Milva knew it wasn't yet. Reluctantly, Geralt allowed Regis to tend to the severe leg injury, allowing the others to see the severity of the situation. He treated it with some kind of paste. Regis asked if Geralt considered him "friend or enemy," noting that most witchers wouldn't hesitate to kill him. Geralt replied that he hadn't decided. He also asked what the bounty would need to be for Geralt to accept a contract on him. Geralt replied it would have to be very high, but immediately doubted anyone could afford such a sum, essentially admitting he had no intention of killing him. He wouldn't say that Regis is an ordinary vampire, and he doubted anyone could pay the reward. Regis finds it odd that an ordinary witcher wouldn't even think twice before trying to kill him. He observed that Geralt is in a state of confusion, experiencing emotions he would typically ignore. He's becoming something else, something new, something more than just a mutated monster hunter. 


This time, he was about to leave when Zoltan invited him to stay and share his story. Regis agreed. First, to reassure everyone, he stated that he no longer enjoyed drinking blood as he once had. He then began introducing himself again as Emiel Regis Rohellec Terzieff-Godefroy, who, he claimed, was currently 428 years old. He share how in vampire society most them take whatever they want because of their gift of immortality. If they didn't participate, they risked becoming outcasts. In his younger years, he gave in to his worst impulses, noting that the euphoria from fresh human blood was incomparable, leading him to drink to his heart's content. His life changed when he met a human woman named Betháne. For her, he stopped drinking blood. They lived a better life, where Regis didn't associate with other vampires. But when she disappeared, he went looking for her, only discovered too late that his fellow vampires had taken her. His coven caused him to lose control, and he killed his fellow vampires, but the worst thing he remembers is Betháne witnessing his horrific acts in her final moments, dying in terrified, seeing him as a monster rather than the man he tried to become for her. Because of the presence of vampires, a mob of villagers beheaded him and buried him. But vampires can regenerate from almost any wound and it took a lot more than that to kill a vampire properly. He remained buried for 50 years, tormented by his terrible mistakes, putting his body back together underground. And so he never drank blood again. 

After this, the group sits down to eat the soup. While they do, Milva suggests that Cahir tell them about his story, insisting that they have listened to everyone else's regrets and so that Geralt can see things from his perspective. Cahir frequently insists to the group that he is not Nilfgaardian and clarifies that he is from Vicovaro, a place very close to Nilfgaard.

Cahir recounts how he had a purpose: to work directly for emperor. As a child, he was abused by his brutal father, which instilled a sense of purpose and a desire to be strong. He met an elder sorcerer who did him a favor for a friend. He spent weeks bringing him food and water in the woods, never seeing the sorcerer's mysterious friend. Until one day, bandits tried to rob him, when he was saved by a spiky, hedgehog-like monster. Over time, he forgot it as if it had never happened, until years later, not long after entering the Nilfgaardian army, Emhyr sought him out, thanking him for his help all those years before entrusting him with the crucial mission to bring back Ciri. It was then that Cahir understood that Emhyr was the "Hedgehog Man" from his past.

Upon hearing Cahir's tale, a shocking truth came to light. Geralt was stunned and angry, for it reminded him of someone he knew as a hedgehog. He explained to the group that the Hedgehog Man from before was named Duny, that he was under a curse and whom Geralt saved during the banquet in Cintra where Pavetta's pregnancy with Ciri was revealed. From Cahir's description, Geralt, connects the dots, finally understood the truth: whom he knew as Duny was none other than Emhyr var Emreis, who was indeed Ciri's father. The shocking truth is that Emhyr intends to marry and father an heir with his own daughter, and fulfill Ithlinne's prophecy. 

Cahir asserts they are bound by destiny. All of them. That it has led them to this very moment. Geralt, however, struggles with this. He has always tried to deny the destiny he didn't always believe in, which he did by denying Ciri's existence.

He walks away alone through the woods, and Geralt recalls a memory with Ciri from their time at Kaer Morhen. He combs Ciri's hair and tells her how, as a child, he dreamed of being a knight. Geralt of Rivia isn't a proper honorific title; he chose it himself to secure better contracts. Although it was a much better choice than the first: his original, more pretentious choice was "Geralt Roger Eric du Haute-Bellegarde". This made Ciri laugh, just as had Vesemir. Ciri observes that knights must trust their sovereigns, prompting Geralt to admit he trusts no one, believing that trust generates emotions witchers should not possess. Ciri argues that trusting people can lead to wonderful things, pointing to the trust she places in Geralt by allowing him to care for her, specifically brushing her hair. She jokingly dubs him a knight in this intimate moment.

The next day, after reflecting on it, Geralt finally decides to accept his group of friends. To Geralt's surprise, though also to his annoyance, Milva revealed that she lied about the river flooding earlier so they could all get a good night's rest. The united group sets off on their journey.[29]

### Facing Rusalka Spirits[]

### Facing Rusalka Spirits[]

In a ruined building atop a hill, Geralt and his company are planning their next route to Nilfgaard. Cahir, who knows these lands well, takes the lead. He suggests crossing through the forests, but Geralt says there's no other option but to cross the swamps, as the Aldiss Pass is heavily guarded by northern soldiers who are cutting timber for the war effort. They all agree to take the swamp route. Suddenly, Milva reveals to the group that she's pregnant as a result of her time with the Scoia'tael unit. Regis, of course, already knew, having sensed the second heartbeat through his vampiric instincts. Milva will have to decide what to do. The group then starts talking at once about what to do, with Milva needing to decide whether to keep the child or terminate the pregnancy. But she silences them, as she not wanted their opinions to help her make her own choice.

Upon entering the Ysgith swamp, Geralt and Cahir finally talk, and Cahir speaks about Ciri's dreams. He says he saw her kill, with blood on her lips, smiling, and darkness in her eyes. He asks if Geralt is worried that Ciri is no longer the young he swore to protect. Geralt doesn't answer, but he is concerned that she might be in such a dark place.

Suddenly, Geralt begins to hear whispering voices calling his name, but the others in the group don't hear them. Then, in an instant, Yarpen, Zoltan, and Percy are grabbed and dragged into the water by a mysterious creature. The rest run back after them, but they can't find them. Geralt hears the voices again, and they all notice the trees moving, as if the swamp is alive, opening a path for them. They decide to cross it, guided by the voice of a little girl speaking to Geralt, to find their friends. They search for the dwarves and the gnome, while Regis finds a special plant for Milva to help with her problem. However, their conversation is interrupted when the creature takes Cahir and Jaskier, leaving Geralt, Regis, and Milva alone. Geralt asks the voice or creature what it wants, and realizing it wants him, another path opens up. The group has no choice but to follow it.

Since Geralt appears to be the target of the creature in his game, he decides to go alone, because it only wants him. Milva isn't entirely convinced he should go; she thinks he's giving in to her demands, although Regis agrees with Geralt's decision. 

Geralt tries to go alone to find the creature, but he is plagued by visions when he hears and believes he sees Ciri dying in Yennefer's arms on a nearby island. He struggles to get closer to them, until Regis and Milva reach him and pull him out of the illusion, after hearing his cries. Geralt swears it was Yennefer and Ciri. He felt it. But Milva and Regis correct him that what he saw wasn't real. Milva even rebukes him for almost walking into a trap. Regis then suggests that together they are stronger, despite what he said earlier about it being Geralt's decision, but that his decision shouldn't preclude others from making their own.

Then Geralt hears their friends calling for help nearby, and they reach a clearing, just as the creature snatches Milva and Regis up into the trees, leaving Geralt alone once more to face it. He sees something climbing and running through the trees. The creature arrives and leaps to confront Geralt. The creature is a girl covered in vines, and from beneath the water emerges another, her mother. They are spirits called Rusalkas that haunt the swamp. There, Geralt notices his friends trapped beneath the surface, trapped in their worst fears. He is quickly subdued when he tries to attack the mother with his sword. He demands she tell him the riddle, knowing that if he solves it, he and his friends will be freed. The Rusalka mother gives it to him without hesitation: "What I love, I do not carry. What I nurture, I do not feed. What I live and die for is not mine alone. What am I?"


Geralt thinks, but doesn't answer, so the Rusalka mother lets her daughter play with her friends, while she lies beside her, telling him she "missed" him. Geralt then tricks the mother's spirit into approaching and seizes the opportunity to attack the daughter, causing the mother to drag Geralt into the water with lialas trying to submerge him. As the spirits moan and cry, Geralt manages to see their past human forms: the mother and daughter were trapped in the swamp and died waiting for the father figure to arrive and rescue them. His presence causes Geralt to hallucinate Yennefer and Ciri, and when the Rusalka tries to drown him, Geralt finally correctly deduced that the answer to the riddle is "Father." Having correctly predicted the riddle, the Rusalkas disappear, revealing the remains of their skeletal bodies where they died, freeing Geralt's group from the swamp water, and also Milva and Regis. Geralt recounted that what he saw was the story of the mother and daughter, not his own; explaining they were Rusalkas haunting the water where they died, struggling to find their family, a quest they couldn't complete. They all then notice that Regis transformed into a bat, guiding them out of the swamp. 

Once settled in the woods, Percival and Zoltan gifts Geralt with Zoltan's sihil as a token of their gratitude, adding, "This sword belongs to Geralt of Rivia, defender of dwarves. May it whistle for a just cause." Yarpen then announces he will return to Mahakam. He says he saw his death in the water below and decides to no longer risk his life, leaving the conflict behind to start a new life. He has a fiancée at home waiting to marry him. Percy goes for practically the same reasons and also decides he has seen enough death, choosing to leave with Yarpen in search of a better life. Geralt and the others wish him well and bid him farewell.

That night, Geralt and Milva have an intimate conversation. She tells him how her father once showned her caterpillars that ate their cocoons from the inside, a metaphor for how she feels being pregnant. Too distraught to make a decision about her unborn child, Milva shares her anguish with Geralt and reveals that her real name is Maria. She tells him that the baby is devouring the warrior Milva from within; perhaps all that will remain is Maria, who could be a mother. Geralt tries to comfort her by telling her how, as a witcher, he too was drawn into relationships and responsibilities he didn't choose, but which profoundly shaped him and became an essential part of his identity. Ciri and Yennefer changed him for the better. After this intimate conversation, Milva decides to keep the child.


Geralt was heading back to the others when he saw a portal open, from which Yennefer emerged. The two embraced and they were reunited, having last seen each other since she healed him in Brokilon. Geralt expressed his concern to Yennefer about what had happened, to which she replied that she and the other sorceresses fought a battle against Vilgefortz and defeated his mages, although Vilgefortz himself escaped and was still alive. To his surprise and relief, Yennefer revealed that she discovered that Ciri wasn't with Emhyr. So they discovered that the "Ciri" currently in Nilfgaard was the young Teryn, the fake Ciri. Despite the bleak situation, Yennefer expresses deep fear that they may never find Ciri. Geralt reassures her that they would, as he had been dreaming about Ciri. The two go to a secluded part of the woods, entering a small tent that Yennefer conjures, making it appear much larger on the inside. During this encounter, while they bathe together, Yennefer shares the devastating news of the losses she and the other suffered against Vilgefortz and his mages. Geralt comforts her upon hearing of Istredd's loss. But when he learns that Vesemir also died during the battle, having done what Geralt would have done, he is deeply affected by the loss of Vesemir, as he was a paternal figure to him, though remains silent. Geralt and Yennefer then kiss and have sex. 

In the morning, Geralt shares with Yennefer about the dream he had in which he lived happily with her and Ciri as a family, and his and Yennefer's deaths being of old age. When he thinks of a life well-lived, he thinks of them, of his family, until the very end. They both know that perhaps that life will never come, but hope remains between them. Yennefer is surprised by the compassion Geralt has developed and how much he has truly changed, and she also jokes with him about his new friends.

They rejoin the others. Now that they know Ciri isn't in Nilfgaard, Geralt and his company ponder how to find her and where to go. Regis suggests searching for druids. Despite Geralt's initial hesitation, Yennefer urges him to act on this suggestion. Regis proposes seeking out a circle of druids in Caed Dhu, explaining that, with the Equinox approaching, the druids can channel celestial power to locate Ciri. Everyone prepares to leave, while Yennefer must return to Montecalvo with the survivors. Before parting, Yennefer and Geralt share a tender farewell, with a kiss, promising to reunite and finding their daughter.[30]

### Protecting the Bridge[]

Geralt's company searches for a way to cross the Yaruga River to locate the druids. Milva is not with them, having become separated from them to stay with the child. They soon find a ferry thanks to Jaskier, and two cowering ferrymen who were hiding in the bushes Cahir discovered. They manage to convince them to take them to the other side of the river, despite one of the men's insistence that there are "baboon attacks" on the opposite bank. They start to go across when not baboons, but guerrillas, northern soldiers trapped behind enemy lines at that on the other side since there are multiple ones fighting Nilfgaard. The Northern Soldiers yell at Geralt and company to bring the ferry over to them now since they want to escape to the other side. The northerners try to take the boat, but one of the ferrymen panics and cuts the rope. The northerners believe them to be Nilfgaardian spies and open fire with crossbows, as the group rows away and head down the river.

As they go down the river, archers appear on the northern side, Nilfgaardian, who start firing arrows at them. One arrow hits one of the boatman, who falls into the water, and the last one left accuses the group of getting them into this mess. Lucky for them, Milva comes out of nowhere to save them. She took out the archers from behind. Then she dives off a cliff into the water and swims to the ferry to join her friends. 

## Notes[]

  * Geralt was made bald in _The Witcher: Nightmare of the Wolf_ as a kid to hide the fact that it was him until the end, as his white hair would be a dead giveaway.[31]
